<h1 id="mistral-ai-api">Mistral AI API v1.0.0</h1>

> Scroll down for code samples, example requests and responses. Select a language for code samples from the tabs above or the mobile navigation menu.

Our Chat Completion and Embeddings APIs specification. Create your account on [La Plateforme](https://console.mistral.ai) to get access and read the [docs](https://docs.mistral.ai) to learn how to use it.

Base URLs:

* <a href="https://api.mistral.ai">https://api.mistral.ai</a> - Production server

# Authentication

* API Key (DashboardUserContextAuth)
    - Parameter Name: **x-api-key**, in: header. Public API key. The gateway validates the key and forwards authenticated user context to the dashboard.

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: bearer Bearer token. The gateway validates the token and forwards authenticated user context to the dashboard.

* API Key (DashboardUserOrServiceAccountContextAuth)
    - Parameter Name: **x-api-key**, in: header. Public API key. The gateway validates the key and forwards authenticated user context to the dashboard.

* API Key (DashboardContextAuth)
    - Parameter Name: **x-api-key**, in: header. Public API key. The gateway validates the key and forwards authenticated user context to the dashboard.

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: bearer Admin-scoped API key passed as a bearer token. Standard workspace/inference API keys are rejected.

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: bearer

<h1 id="mistral-ai-api-chat">chat</h1>

Chat Completion API.

## Chat Completion

<a id="opIdchat_completion_v1_chat_completions_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mistral.ai/v1/chat/completions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "model": "mistral-large-latest",
    "messages": [
      {
        "role": "user",
        "content": "Who is the best French painter? Answer in one short sentence."
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /v1/chat/completions`

Chat Completion

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "model": "mistral-large-latest",
  "messages": [
    {
      "role": "user",
      "content": "Who is the best French painter? Answer in one short sentence."
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="chat-completion-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[ChatCompletionRequest](#schemachatcompletionrequest)|true|none|
|» model|body|string|true|ID of the model to use. You can use the [List Available Models](/api/#tag/models/operation/list_models_v1_models_get) API to see all of your available models, or see our [Model overview](/models) for model descriptions.|
|» temperature|body|number \| null|false|What sampling temperature to use, we recommend between 0.0 and 0.7. Higher values like 0.7 will make the output more random, while lower values like 0.2 will make it more focused and deterministic. We generally recommend altering this or `top_p` but not both. The default value varies depending on the model you are targeting. Call the `/models` endpoint to retrieve the appropriate value.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|number|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» top_p|body|number \| null|false|Nucleus sampling, where the model considers the results of the tokens with `top_p` probability mass. So 0.1 means only the tokens comprising the top 10% probability mass are considered. We generally recommend altering this or `temperature` but not both.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|number|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» max_tokens|body|integer \| null|false|The maximum number of tokens to generate in the completion. The token count of your prompt plus `max_tokens` cannot exceed the model's context length.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|integer|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» stream|body|boolean|false|Whether to stream back partial progress. If set, tokens will be sent as data-only server-side events as they become available, with the stream terminated by a data: [DONE] message. Otherwise, the server will hold the request open until the timeout or until completion, with the response containing the full result as JSON.|

Setting to `{ "type": "json_object" }` enables JSON mode, which guarantees the message the model generates is in JSON. When using JSON mode you MUST also instruct the model to produce JSON yourself with a system or a user message. Setting to `{ "type": "json_schema" }` enables JSON schema mode, which guarantees the message the model generates is in JSON and follows the schema you provide. <h1 id="mistral-ai-api-responses">responses</h1>

Stateless Responses API for text, images, reasoning, function calls, and streaming.

```bash
    "top_logprobs": 0
  }'
```

`POST /v1/responses`

Create a response.

Generate a model response from text, image, or file inputs. The response can
include text, reasoning, and function calls. Set stream to true to
receive Server-Sent Events.

For multi-turn conversations, send the full history in input, including
prior output items and function results. Responses are not stored. Only
client-executed function tools are supported.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "model": "string",
  "input": "string",
  "instructions": "string",
  "parallel_tool_calls": true,
  "previous_response_id": null,
  "truncation": "disabled",
  "tools": [
    {
      "name": "string",
      "parameters": null,
      "strict": null,
      "type": "function",
      "allowed_callers": null,
      "async": null,
      "defer_loading": null,
      "description": null,
      "output_schema": null
    }
  ],
  "tool_choice": "auto",
  "reasoning": {
    "effort": null
  },
  "conversation": null,
  "prompt": null,
  "text": {
    "format": null,
    "verbosity": null
  },
  "background": false,
  "stream": false,

  "max_output_tokens": 1,
  "temperature": 0,

    "property2": "string"
  },

  "top_logprobs": 0
}
```

`POST /v1/responses/input_tokens`

Count response input tokens.

Count the input tokens for a Responses request without generating a
response. The count includes the supplied conversation, instructions,
and tool definitions.

Use the same input, instructions, and tools that you plan to send when
creating a response. For multi-turn conversations, include prior output
items and function results in input.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "model": "string",
  "input": "string",
  "instructions": "string",
  "parallel_tool_calls": true,
  "previous_response_id": null,
  "truncation": "disabled",
  "tools": [
    {
      "name": "string",
      "parameters": null,
      "strict": null,
      "type": "function",
      "allowed_callers": null,
      "async": null,
      "defer_loading": null,
      "description": null,
      "output_schema": null
    }
  ],
  "tool_choice": "auto",
  "reasoning": {
    "effort": null
  },
  "conversation": null,
  "prompt": null,
  "text": {
    "format": null,
    "verbosity": null
  }
}
```

<h1 id="mistral-ai-api-fim">fim</h1>

Fill-in-the-middle API.

## Fim Completion

<a id="opIdfim_completion_v1_fim_completions_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mistral.ai/v1/fim/completions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "model": "codestral-latest",
    "temperature": 0,
    "top_p": 0.1,
    "max_tokens": 0,
    "stream": false,
    "stop": "string",
    "random_seed": 0,
    "metadata": {},
    "prompt": "def",
    "suffix": "return a+b",
    "min_tokens": 0,
    "prompt_cache_key": "string"
  }'
```

Higher values like 0.7 will make the output more random, while lower values like 0.2 will make it more focused and deterministic. We generally recommend altering this or `top_p` but not both. The default value varies depending on the model you are targeting. Call the `/models` endpoint to retrieve the appropriate value.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|number|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» top_p|body|number \| null|false|Nucleus sampling, where the model considers the results of the tokens with `top_p` probability mass. So 0.1 means only the tokens comprising the top 10% probability mass are considered. We generally recommend altering this or `temperature` but not both.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|number|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» max_tokens|body|integer \| null|false|The maximum number of tokens to generate in the completion. The token count of your prompt plus `max_tokens` cannot exceed the model's context length.|

|» suffix|body|string \| null|false|Optional text/code that adds more context for the model. When given a `prompt` and a `suffix` the model will fill what is between them. When `suffix` is not provided, the model will simply execute completion starting with `prompt`.|

## Upload File

<a id="opIdfiles_api_routes_upload_file"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mistral.ai/v1/files \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -F 'purpose=batch' \
  -F 'file=@/path/to/file'
```

`POST /v1/files`

Upload a file that can be used across various endpoints.

The size of individual files can be a maximum of 512 MB.

Please contact us if you need to increase these storage limits.

> Body parameter

```yaml
purpose: batch
file: example.file
```

<h3 id="upload-file-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» expiry|body|integer \| null|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|integer|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» visibility|body|object|false|none|
|» purpose|body|[FilePurpose](#schemafilepurpose)|false|none|
|» file|body|[File](#schemafile)|true|The File object (not file name) to be uploaded.<br> To upload a file and specify a custom file name you should format your request as such:<br> ```bash<br> file=@path/to/your/file.jsonl;filename=custom_name.jsonl<br> ```<br> Otherwise, you can just keep the original file name:<br> ```bash<br> file=@path/to/your/file.jsonl<br> ```|

#### Enumerated Values

|» purpose|fine-tune|
|» purpose|batch|
|» purpose|ocr|
|» purpose|agentic_safety|

## Create Batch Job

<a id="opIdjobs_api_routes_batch_create_batch_job"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mistral.ai/v1/batch/jobs \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "input_files": [
      "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
    ],
    "requests": [
      {
        "custom_id": "string",
        "body": {}
      }
    ],
    "endpoint": "/v1/chat/completions",
    "model": "mistral-small-latest",
    "agent_id": "string",
    "metadata": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    },
    "timeout_hours": 24
  }'
```

`POST /v1/batch/jobs`

Create a new batch job, it will be queued for processing.

```json
    "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
```

|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|

|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» metadata|body|object \| null|false|The metadata of your choice to be associated with the batch inference job.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» timeout_hours|body|integer|false|The timeout in hours for the batch inference job.|

```json
      "markdown": "# LEVERAGING UNLABELED DATA TO PREDICT OUT-OF-DISTRIBUTION PERFORMANCE\nSaurabh Garg*<br> Carnegie Mellon University<br> sgarg2@andrew.cmu.edu<br> Sivaraman Balakrishnan<br> Carnegie Mellon University<br> sbalakri@andrew.cmu.edu<br> Zachary C. Lipton<br> Carnegie Mellon University<br> zlipton@andrew.cmu.edu\n## Behnam Neyshabur\nGoogle Research, Blueshift team<br> neyshabur@google.com\nHanie Sedghi<br> Google Research, Brain team<br> hsedghi@google.com\n#### Abstract\nReal-world machine learning deployments are characterized by mismatches between the source (training) and target (test) distributions that may cause performance drops. In this work, we investigate methods for predicting the target domain accuracy using only labeled source data and unlabeled target data. We propose Average Thresholded Confidence (ATC), a practical method that learns a threshold on the model's confidence, predicting accuracy as the fraction of unlabeled examples for which model confidence exceeds that threshold. ATC outperforms previous methods across several model architectures, types of distribution shifts (e.g., due to synthetic corruptions, dataset reproduction, or novel subpopulations), and datasets (WILDS, ImageNet, BREEDS, CIFAR, and MNIST). In our experiments, ATC estimates target performance $2-4 \\times$ more accurately than prior methods. We also explore the theoretical foundations of the problem, proving that, in general, identifying the accuracy is just as hard as identifying the optimal predictor and thus, the efficacy of any method rests upon (perhaps unstated) assumptions on the nature of the shift. Finally, analyzing our method on some toy distributions, we provide insights concerning when it works ${ }^{1}$.\n## 1 INTRODUCTION\nMachine learning models deployed in the real world typically encounter examples from previously unseen distributions. While the IID assumption enables us to evaluate models using held-out data from the source distribution (from which training data is sampled), this estimate is no longer valid in presence of a distribution shift. Moreover, under such shifts, model accuracy tends to degrade (Szegedy et al., 2014; Recht et al., 2019; Koh et al., 2021). Commonly, the only data available to the practitioner are a labeled training set (source) and unlabeled deployment-time data which makes the problem more difficult. In this setting, detecting shifts in the distribution of covariates is known to be possible (but difficult) in theory (Ramdas et al., 2015), and in practice (Rabanser et al., 2018). However, producing an optimal predictor using only labeled source and unlabeled target data is well-known to be impossible absent further assumptions (Ben-David et al., 2010; Lipton et al., 2018).\nTwo vital questions that remain are: (i) the precise conditions under which we can estimate a classifier's target-domain accuracy; and (ii) which methods are most practically useful. To begin, the straightforward way to assess the performance of a model under distribution shift would be to collect labeled (target domain) examples and then to evaluate the model on that data. However, collecting fresh labeled data from the target distribution is prohibitively expensive and time-consuming, especially if the target distribution is non-stationary. Hence, instead of using labeled data, we aim to use unlabeled data from the target distribution, that is comparatively abundant, to predict model performance. Note that in this work, our focus is not to improve performance on the target but, rather, to estimate the accuracy on the target for a given classifier.\n[^0]: Work done in part while Saurabh Garg was interning at Google ${ }^{1}$ Code is available at [https://github.com/saurabhgarg1996/ATC_code](https://github.com/saurabhgarg1996/ATC_code).\n",

        "height": 2200,
        "width": 1700
      }
    },
    {
      "index": 2,
      "markdown": "![img-0.jpeg](img-0.jpeg)\nFigure 1: Illustration of our proposed method ATC. Left: using source domain validation data, we identify a threshold on a score (e.g. negative entropy) computed on model confidence such that fraction of examples above the threshold matches the validation set accuracy. ATC estimates accuracy on unlabeled target data as the fraction of examples with the score above the threshold. Interestingly, this threshold yields accurate estimates on a wide set of target distributions resulting from natural and synthetic shifts. Right: Efficacy of ATC over previously proposed approaches on our testbed with a post-hoc calibrated model. To obtain errors on the same scale, we rescale all errors with Average Confidence (AC) error. Lower estimation error is better. See Table 1 for exact numbers and comparison on various types of distribution shift. See Sec. 5 for details on our testbed.\nRecently, numerous methods have been proposed for this purpose (Deng & Zheng, 2021; Chen et al., 2021b; Jiang et al., 2021; Deng et al., 2021; Guillory et al., 2021). These methods either require calibration on the target domain to yield consistent estimates (Jiang et al., 2021; Guillory et al., 2021) or additional labeled data from several target domains to learn a linear regression function on a distributional distance that then predicts model performance (Deng et al., 2021; Deng & Zheng, 2021; Guillory et al., 2021). However, methods that require calibration on the target domain typically yield poor estimates since deep models trained and calibrated on source data are not, in general, calibrated on a (previously unseen) target domain (Ovadia et al., 2019). Besides, methods that leverage labeled data from target domains rely on the fact that unseen target domains exhibit strong linear correlation with seen target domains on the underlying distance measure and, hence, can be rendered ineffective when such target domains with labeled data are unavailable (in Sec. 5.1 we demonstrate such a failure on a real-world distribution shift problem). Therefore, throughout the paper, we assume access to labeled source data and only unlabeled data from target domain(s).\nIn this work, we first show that absent assumptions on the source classifier or the nature of the shift, no method of estimating accuracy will work generally (even in non-contrived settings). To estimate accuracy on target domain perfectly, we highlight that even given perfect knowledge of the labeled source distribution (i.e., $p_{s}(x, y)$ ) and unlabeled target distribution (i.e., $p_{t}(x)$ ), we need restrictions on the nature of the shift such that we can uniquely identify the target conditional $p_{t}(y \\mid x)$. Thus, in general, identifying the accuracy of the classifier is as hard as identifying the optimal predictor.\nSecond, motivated by the superiority of methods that use maximum softmax probability (or logit) of a model for Out-Of-Distribution (OOD) detection (Hendrycks & Gimpel, 2016; Hendrycks et al., 2019), we propose a simple method that leverages softmax probability to predict model performance. Our method, Average Thresholded Confidence (ATC), learns a threshold on a score (e.g., maximum confidence or negative entropy) of model confidence on validation source data and predicts target domain accuracy as the fraction of unlabeled target points that receive a score above that threshold. ATC selects a threshold on validation source data such that the fraction of source examples that receive the score above the threshold match the accuracy of those examples. Our primary contribution in ATC is the proposal of obtaining the threshold and observing its efficacy on (practical) accuracy estimation. Importantly, our work takes a step forward in positively answering the question raised in Deng & Zheng (2021); Deng et al. (2021) about a practical strategy to select a threshold that enables accuracy prediction with thresholded model confidence.\n",
```

<h1 id="mistral-ai-api-audiotranscriptions">audio.transcriptions</h1>

API for audio transcription.

## Create Transcription

<a id="opIdaudio_api_v1_transcriptions_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mistral.ai/v1/audio/transcriptions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -F 'model=voxtral-mini-latest' \
  -F 'file=' \
  -F 'file_url=' \
  -F 'file_id=' \
  -F 'language=' \
  -F 'temperature=' \
  -F 'stream=false' \
  -F 'diarize=false' \
  -F 'context_bias=[]' \
  -F 'speaker_references={"property1":"string","property2":"string"}' \
  -F 'timestamp_granularities=["segment"]'
```

`POST /v1/audio/transcriptions`

Create Transcription

> Body parameter

```yaml
model: voxtral-mini-latest
file: null
file_url: null
file_id: null
language: null
temperature: null
stream: false
diarize: false
context_bias: []
speaker_references:
  property1: string
  property2: string
timestamp_granularities:
  - segment
```

<h3 id="create-transcription-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[AudioTranscriptionRequest](#schemaaudiotranscriptionrequest)|true|none|
|» model|body|string|true|ID of the model to be used.|
|» file|body|[File](#schemafile) \| null|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[File](#schemafile)|false|The File object (not file name) to be uploaded.<br> To upload a file and specify a custom file name you should format your request as such:<br> ```bash<br> file=@path/to/your/file.jsonl;filename=custom_name.jsonl<br> ```<br> Otherwise, you can just keep the original file name:<br> ```bash<br> file=@path/to/your/file.jsonl<br> ```|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» file_url|body|string(uri) \| null|false|Url of a file to be transcribed|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string(uri)|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» file_id|body|string \| null|false|ID of a file uploaded to /v1/files|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» language|body|string \| null|false|Language of the audio, e.g. 'en'. Providing the language can boost accuracy.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» temperature|body|number \| null|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|number|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» stream|body|boolean|false|none|
|» diarize|body|boolean|false|none|
|» context_bias|body|[string]|false|none|
|» speaker_references|body|object|false|Dictionary of speaker names and reference audios for speakers who are known to appear in the audio. When enabled, diarize must be true. Predicted speakers will be matched against reference speakers from this dictionary.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» timestamp_granularities|body|[[TimestampGranularity](#schematimestampgranularity)]|false|Granularities of timestamps to include in the response.|

<a id="opIdagents_api_v1_agents_list"></a>

```bash
curl https://api.mistral.ai/v1/agents \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/agents`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Retrieve a list of agent entities sorted by creation time. Deprecated: some features such as agent sharing are not supported by this endpoint. Use the cursor-paginated `GET /v1/agents/pages` instead.

<h3 id="list-agent-entities-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|page|query|integer|false|Page number (0-indexed)|
|page_size|query|integer|false|Number of agents per page|
|deployment_chat|query|boolean \| null|false|none|
|sources|query|[[RequestSource](#schemarequestsource)] \| null|false|none|
|name|query|string \| null|false|Filter by agent name|
|search|query|string \| null|false|Search agents by name or ID|
|id|query|string \| null|false|none|
|metadata|query|object \| null|false|none|

## List agent entities, cursor-paginated.

<a id="opIdagents_api_v1_agents_list_pages"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mistral.ai/v1/agents/pages \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/agents/pages`

Retrieve a page of agent entities. Unlike the deprecated `GET /v1/agents`, this endpoint paginates by opaque cursor and honors per-agent sharing, returning only agents the caller is authorized to see.

<h3 id="list-agent-entities-cursor-paginated-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page_size|query|integer|false|Number of agents per page|
|deployment_chat|query|boolean \| null|false|none|
|sources|query|[[RequestSource](#schemarequestsource)] \| null|false|none|
|name|query|string \| null|false|Filter by agent name|
|search|query|string \| null|false|Search agents by name or ID|
|id|query|string \| null|false|none|
|metadata|query|object \| null|false|none|
|page_token|query|string \| null|false|Opaque cursor from a previous response's next_page_token. When set, results page forward from the cursor.|

## Create a conversation and append entries to it.

<a id="opIdagents_api_v1_conversations_start"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mistral.ai/v1/conversations \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "inputs": "string",
    "stream": false,
    "store": null,
    "handoff_execution": null,
    "instructions": null,
    "tools": null,
    "completion_args": null,
    "guardrails": null,
    "name": null,
    "description": null,
    "metadata": null,
    "agent_id": null,
    "agent_version": null,
    "model": null
  }'
```

`POST /v1/conversations`

Create a new conversation, using a base model or an agent and append entries. Completion and tool executions are run and the response is appended to the conversation.Use the returned conversation_id to continue the conversation.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "inputs": "string",
  "stream": false,
  "store": null,
  "handoff_execution": null,
  "instructions": null,
  "tools": null,
  "completion_args": null,
  "guardrails": null,
  "name": null,
  "description": null,
  "metadata": null,
  "agent_id": null,
  "agent_version": null,
  "model": null
}
```

|» » *anyOf*|body|[[FunctionTool](#schemafunctiontool) \| [WebSearchTool](#schemawebsearchtool) \| [WebSearchPremiumTool](#schemawebsearchpremiumtool) \| [CodeInterpreterTool](#schemacodeinterpretertool) \| [ImageGenerationTool](#schemaimagegenerationtool) \| [DocumentLibraryTool](#schemadocumentlibrarytool) \| [CustomConnector](#schemacustomconnector)]|false|none|

## Upload a new document.

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mistral.ai/v1/libraries/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/documents \
  -X POST \

  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -F 'file=@/path/to/file'
```

`POST /v1/libraries/{library_id}/documents`

Given a library, upload a new document to that library. It is queued for processing, it status will change it has been processed. The processing has to be completed in order be discoverable for the library search

## Create or update an access level.

<a id="opIdlibraries_share_create_v1"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mistral.ai/v1/libraries/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/share \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "org_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "level": "Viewer",
    "share_with_uuid": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "share_with_type": "User"
  }'
```

`PUT /v1/libraries/{library_id}/share`

Given a library id, you can create or update the access level of an entity. You have to be owner of the library to share a library. An owner cannot change their own role. A library cannot be shared outside of the organization.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "org_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "level": "Viewer",
  "share_with_uuid": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "share_with_type": "User"
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|» org_id|body|string(uuid) \| null|false|**Deprecated.**|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string(uuid)|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» level|body|[ShareEnum](#schemashareenum)|true|none|
|» share_with_uuid|body|string(uuid)|true|The id of the user or workspace to share with|
|» share_with_type|body|[EntityType](#schemaentitytype)|true|The type of entity, used to share a library.|

## Delete an access level.

<a id="opIdlibraries_share_delete_v1"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mistral.ai/v1/libraries/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/share \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "org_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",

    "share_with_type": "User"
  }'
```

`DELETE /v1/libraries/{library_id}/share`

Given a library id, you can delete the access level of an entity. An owner cannot delete their own access. You have to be the owner of the library to delete an access other than yours. Warning: the response will change from 200 (returning the deleted sharing) to 204 No Content in a future version.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "org_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "share_with_uuid": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "share_with_type": "User"
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|library_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|body|body|[SharingDelete](#schemasharingdelete)|true|none|
|» org_id|body|string(uuid) \| null|false|**Deprecated.**|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string(uuid)|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» share_with_uuid|body|string(uuid)|true|The id of the entity to stop sharing with, as returned by the list endpoint|
|» share_with_type|body|[EntityType](#schemaentitytype)|true|The type of entity, used to share a library.|

## Get the auth URL for a connector.

<a id="opIdconnector_get_auth_url_v1"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mistral.ai/v1/connectors/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/auth_url \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/connectors/{connector_id_or_name}/auth_url`

Get the OAuth2 authorization URL for a connector to initiate user authentication.

<h3 id="get-the-auth-url-for-a-connector-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|connector_id_or_name|path|string(uuid) \| string|true|none|
|app_return_url|query|string \| null|false|none|
|method_type|query|[AuthenticationType](#schemaauthenticationtype)|false|Auth method type to use for the authorization URL. Required when the connector supports multiple interactive auth methods; otherwise the sole method is selected automatically. Use this to pick a specific method (e.g. 'oauth2' vs 'github_app').|
|credentials_name|query|string \| null|false|none|
|credentials_title|query|string \| null|false|none|
|github_installation_link|query|boolean|false|Only valid with method_type=oauth2. When true, returns a GitHub App installation URL (https://github.com/apps/&lt;slug&gt;/installations/new) if the connector has the proper configuration The Github application needs to have 'Request user authorization (OAuth) during installation' enabled to perform the proper auth loop.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|method_type|oauth2|
|method_type|bearer|
|method_type|none|
|method_type|github_app|
|method_type|slack_app|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "auth_url": "string",
  "ttl": 0
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
  "detail": [
    {
      "loc": [
        "string"
      ],
      "msg": "string",
      "type": "string",
      "input": null,
      "ctx": {}
    }
  ]
}
```

## Share a private connector to the current workspace.

<a id="opIdconnector_share_v1"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mistral.ai/v1/connectors/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/share \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`PUT /v1/connectors/{connector_id}/share`

Transfers ownership of a private user-owned connector to the current workspace, making it available to all workspace members. The creator can later revert this via the unshare endpoint. Any authentication flows that rely on the original owner's identity (e.g. OAuth on-behalf-of) will be affected and must be reconfigured after sharing. Only the connector's creator can call this endpoint. Requires the ShareConnectorToWorkspace workspace permission.

<h3 id="share-a-private-connector-to-the-current-workspace-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|connector_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string"
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "detail": [
    {
      "loc": [
        "string"
      ],
      "msg": "string",
      "type": "string",
      "input": null,
      "ctx": {}
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="share-a-private-connector-to-the-current-workspace-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful Response|[MessageResponse](#schemamessageresponse)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation Error|[HTTPValidationError](#schemahttpvalidationerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ApiKey
</aside>

## Unshare a connector from the current workspace.

<a id="opIdconnector_unshare_v1"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mistral.ai/v1/connectors/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/share \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v1/connectors/{connector_id}/share`

Reverts a workspace-shared connector back to a private, creator-owned connector. Workspace-scoped connections and other members' connections are removed; the creator's own connection is preserved. Only the connector's creator can call this endpoint. Requires the ShareConnectorToWorkspace workspace permission.

<h3 id="unshare-a-connector-from-the-current-workspace-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|connector_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string"
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "detail": [
    {
      "loc": [
        "string"
      ],
      "msg": "string",
      "type": "string",
      "input": null,
      "ctx": {}
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="unshare-a-connector-from-the-current-workspace-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful Response|[MessageResponse](#schemamessageresponse)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation Error|[HTTPValidationError](#schemahttpvalidationerror)|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:

## Invite Users

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mistral.ai/v1/admin/users-invite \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "role_names": [
      "member"
    ],
    "roles": [
      "A"
    ],
    "role_name": "member",
    "role": "A",
    "email": "alice.martin@example.com, bob.smith@example.com",
    "subscription_type": "API",
    "subscription_types": [
      "API"
    ],
    "subscription_seat_automatic_granting": false,
    "email_language": "en",
    "workspace_uuids": [
      "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
    ]
  }'
```

## Deactivate User

<a id="opIdusers_api_admin_users_deactivate_user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mistral.ai/v1/admin/users/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/deactivate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /v1/admin/users/{user_id}/deactivate`

Deactivate a user whose email address is on one of the Organization's verified domains: end their sessions,
delete their API keys and release their seats. Their memberships, groups and roles are kept, so that
`POST /users/{user_id}/reactivate` can give their access back.

<h3 id="deactivate-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|user_id|path|string(uuid)|true|User ID.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "message": "User deactivated successfully"
}
```

<h3 id="deactivate-user-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[DeactivateUserOUT](#schemadeactivateuserout)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
AdminApiKey
</aside>


`PATCH /v1/admin/workspaces/{workspace_uuid}/users`

Add or update Workspace members.

For each member, either set its roles with `roles` or `role_names`, which replaces all the roles it has in
the Workspace, or change them with `add_roles`/`add_role_names` and `remove_roles`/`remove_role_names`,
which keeps its other roles. Users who are not yet members are added with the given roles.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "members": [
    {
      "add_roles": [
        "48436751-ee56-44bd-8a2d-712233977821"
      ],
      "add_role_names": [
        "user"
      ],
      "remove_roles": [
        "578584f1-4319-4c88-9948-38a5184483b6"
      ],
      "remove_role_names": [
        "dev"
      ],
      "role_names": [
        "user"
      ],
      "roles": [
        "A"
      ],
      "role_name": "user",
      "role": "A",
      "user_uuid": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="add-or-update-users-workspaces-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace_uuid|path|string(uuid)|true|Workspace ID.|
|body|body|[AdminWorkspaceMemberUpsertIN](#schemaadminworkspacememberupsertin)|true|none|
|» members|body|[[AdminWorkspaceMemberUpsertSingleIN](#schemaadminworkspacememberupsertsinglein)] \| null|false|Workspace members to add or update. 'roles' or 'role_names' replace the member's roles; 'add_*' and 'remove_*' change them without touching the others.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[[AdminWorkspaceMemberUpsertSingleIN](#schemaadminworkspacememberupsertsinglein)]|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "added_members_count": 0,
  "updated_members_count": 0
}
```

<h3 id="add-or-update-users-workspaces-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[AddOrUpdateUsersToWorkspaceOUT](#schemaaddorupdateuserstoworkspaceout)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
AdminApiKey
</aside>

`POST /v1/admin/usage/query`

Query the organization's detailed usage for a required time range.

Optional filters, caller-selected grouping and time buckets, pagination, aggregates, and distinct API-call counts
are supported. The response contains usage quantities only; it does not include prices, currency, or calculated
costs. For a fixed monthly report with pricing, use `GET /v1/admin/usage`.

`GET /v1/admin/usage`

Return the organization's usage for a calendar month in a fixed, product-oriented format.

The response includes the applicable price catalog and currency. For custom time ranges, filters, grouping, and
pagination, use `POST /v1/admin/usage/query`.

|workspace_id|query|string(uuid) \| null|false|Workspace ID to filter results.|
|api_zone|query|[ApiZone](#schemaapizone) \| null|false|Regional inference zone to filter results.|

## Get User Groups

```bash
curl https://api.mistral.ai/v1/admin/user-groups \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/admin/user-groups`

Get all user groups across the organization.

<h3 id="get-user-groups-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page|query|integer|false|Page number to return.|
|page_size|query|integer|false|Maximum number of results per page.|
|search|query|string \| null|false|Search term used to filter user groups by name.|
|workspace_uuid|query|string(uuid) \| null|false|Filter groups to those assigned to this Workspace. Assignments to archived Workspaces never match.|
|role|query|string \| null|false|Filter groups to those holding this role on a Workspace. When combined with workspace_uuid, the role must be held on that Workspace. Assignments to archived Workspaces never match.|

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "total": 0,
  "items": [

      "name": "Engineering Team",
      "description": "Members of the platform engineering team",
      "externally_managed": true,
      "organization_role": "string"
    }
  ],
  "page": 0,
  "page_size": 0
}
```

## Provision Group To Workspace

<a id="opIdusers_api_admin_user_groups_provision_group_to_workspace"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mistral.ai/v1/admin/user-groups/provision-workspace \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "user_group_uuid": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "workspace_uuid": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "workspace_role": "A",
    "workspace_role_name": "user"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/admin/user-groups/provision-workspace`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Deprecated: provision all users from a user group to a workspace with a specific role.

Use `POST /user-groups/{group_uuid}/workspaces` with `role_names` to assign the group to a workspace, and
`PATCH /user-groups/{group_uuid}/workspaces/{workspace_uuid}` to change the roles of an existing assignment.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "user_group_uuid": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "workspace_uuid": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "workspace_role": "A",
  "workspace_role_name": "user"
}
```

<h3 id="provision-group-to-workspace-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[AdminProvisionGroupToWorkspaceIn](#schemaadminprovisiongrouptoworkspacein)|true|none|
|» user_group_uuid|body|string(uuid)|true|User group ID to provision.|
|» workspace_uuid|body|string(uuid)|true|Workspace ID where the group is provisioned.|
|» workspace_role|body|[WorkspaceRole](#schemaworkspacerole) \| [StaticWorkspaceRoles](#schemastaticworkspaceroles) \| null|false|Workspace role value to assign to the group. Mutually exclusive with 'workspace_role_name'.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[WorkspaceRole](#schemaworkspacerole)|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[StaticWorkspaceRoles](#schemastaticworkspaceroles)|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» workspace_role_name|body|string \| null|false|Workspace role name to assign to the group. Mutually exclusive with 'workspace_role'.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

`PATCH /v1/admin/user-groups/{group_uuid}/workspaces/{workspace_uuid}`

Update the workspace role assignment for a user group.

Either set the group's roles with `role_names` or `roles`, which replaces all the roles it has on the
Workspace, or change them with `add_role_names`/`add_roles` and `remove_role_names`/`remove_roles`, which
keeps its other roles.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "add_roles": [
    "48436751-ee56-44bd-8a2d-712233977821"
  ],
  "add_role_names": [
    "user"
  ],
  "remove_roles": [
    "578584f1-4319-4c88-9948-38a5184483b6"
  ],
  "remove_role_names": [
    "dev"
  ],
  "role_names": [
    "user"
  ],
  "roles": [
    "A"
  ],
  "role": "A"
}
```

`PATCH /v1/audio/sessions/{session_id}`

Update the instructions, tools or turn handling of a live session.

The agent applies the update at its next turn boundary, so it is not yet
applied when this returns.
The agent's `session_updated` and `session_update_failed` webhooks report
the outcome to your server.

```json
  "instructions": "string",

      }
    }
  ],

}
```

<h1 id="mistral-ai-api-betaadminscim">beta.admin.scim</h1>

(beta) Admin - Scim API.

## Trigger Scim Sync

<a id="opIdusers_api_admin_scim_sync_trigger_scim_sync"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mistral.ai/v1/admin/scim/sync \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "dry_run": true,
    "sync_config": {
      "delete_missing_groups": false,
      "deprovision_users": false,
      "sync_groups": true,
      "sync_memberships": true,
      "sync_users": true
    }
  }'
```

`POST /v1/admin/scim/sync`

Trigger an on-demand SCIM synchronization for the Organization.

Requires SAML authentication to be enabled and the Organization to be in SCIM
user provisioning mode. A dry run previews every change without applying it;
a real run applies the categories selected in `sync_config`. Only one run may
be active at a time — a conflicting request returns the already-active run.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "dry_run": true,
  "sync_config": {
    "delete_missing_groups": false,
    "deprovision_users": false,
    "sync_groups": true,
    "sync_memberships": true,
    "sync_users": true
  }
}
```

<h3 id="trigger-scim-sync-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[AdminScimSyncTriggerIN](#schemaadminscimsynctriggerin)|true|none|
|» dry_run|body|boolean|false|Preview all synchronization changes without applying them.|
|» sync_config|body|[AdminScimSyncConfig](#schemaadminscimsyncconfig) \| null|false|Categories to synchronize. Required when dry_run is false; ignored for dry runs.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[AdminScimSyncConfig](#schemaadminscimsyncconfig)|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|

> Example responses

> 202 Response

```json
{
  "run_id": "6f9619ff-8b86-d011-b42d-00cf4fc964ff"
}
```

> 409 Response

```json
{
  "run_id": "6f9619ff-8b86-d011-b42d-00cf4fc964ff",
  "status": "PENDING"
}
```

<h3 id="trigger-scim-sync-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|202|Accepted|Accepted|[AdminScimSyncTriggerOUT](#schemaadminscimsynctriggerout)|
|409|Conflict|Conflict|[AdminScimSyncActiveRunOUT](#schemaadminscimsyncactiverunout)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
AdminApiKey
</aside>

## Get Scim Sync Run

<a id="opIdusers_api_admin_scim_sync_get_scim_sync_run"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mistral.ai/v1/admin/scim/sync/6f9619ff-8b86-d011-b42d-00cf4fc964ff \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/admin/scim/sync/{run_id}`

Retrieve an on-demand SCIM synchronization run for the Organization.

Returns the run's lifecycle status along with the preview or result summary
once the synchronization plan has been built.

## Create a managed index

<a id="opIdcreate_index_v1_context_search_indexes_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mistral.ai/v1/context/search-indexes \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "string",
    "schema": {
      "document_fields": {},
      "chunk_fields": {}
    },
    "config": {
      "embedding": {
        "type": "mistral",
        "name": "string",
        "dtype": "float16",
        "dimensions": 1,
        "distance_metric": "cosine"
      }
    }
  }'
```

`POST /v1/context/search-indexes`

Reserves a managed search index and starts asynchronous backing-table provisioning. Poll the returned Location until status is ready or failed.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "schema": {
    "document_fields": {},
    "chunk_fields": {}
  },
  "config": {
    "embedding": {
      "type": "mistral",
      "name": "string",
      "dtype": "float16",
      "dimensions": 1,
      "distance_metric": "cosine"
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-managed-index-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreateManagedIndexRequest](#schemacreatemanagedindexrequest)|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|none|
|» schema|body|[ManagedIndexFields](#schemamanagedindexfields)|false|none|
|» config|body|[ManagedIndexConfig](#schemamanagedindexconfig)|true|none|

> Example responses

> 202 Response

```json
{
  "id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "name": "string",
  "creator_id": "string",
  "status": "provisioning",
  "status_message": "string",
  "schema": {
    "document_fields": {},
    "chunk_fields": {}
  },
  "config": {
    "embedding": {
      "type": "mistral",
      "name": "string",
      "dtype": "float16",
      "dimensions": 1,
      "distance_metric": "cosine"
    }
  },
  "created_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "modified_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "detail": [
    {
      "loc": [
        "string"
      ],
      "msg": "string",
      "type": "string",
      "input": null,
      "ctx": {}
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-managed-index-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|202|Accepted|Index reserved and queued for provisioning|[ManagedIndexResponse](#schemamanagedindexresponse)|
|403|Forbidden|The organization has reached its index limit, or permission denied|None|
|409|Conflict|An index with the same name already exists|None|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation Error|[HTTPValidationError](#schemahttpvalidationerror)|
|503|Service Unavailable|Temporarily unavailable; retry later|None|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|202|Location|string||Managed-index status resource|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ApiKey
</aside>

## Update a managed index schema

<a id="opIdupdate_index_v1_context_search_indexes__index_name__put"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mistral.ai/v1/context/search-indexes/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "schema": {
      "document_fields": {},
      "chunk_fields": {}
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /v1/context/search-indexes/{index_name}`

Records a new schema for the managed search index and applies it asynchronously. The index keeps serving its current schema until the new one is on disk; poll it until status is ready. Additive only: the new schema must keep every field the current one has.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "schema": {
    "document_fields": {},
    "chunk_fields": {}
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-managed-index-schema-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|index_name|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[UpdateManagedIndexRequest](#schemaupdatemanagedindexrequest)|true|none|
|» schema|body|[ManagedIndexFields](#schemamanagedindexfields)|true|none|

> Example responses

> 202 Response

```json
{
  "id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "name": "string",
  "creator_id": "string",
  "status": "provisioning",
  "status_message": "string",
  "schema": {
    "document_fields": {},
    "chunk_fields": {}
  },
  "config": {
    "embedding": {
      "type": "mistral",
      "name": "string",
      "dtype": "float16",
      "dimensions": 1,
      "distance_metric": "cosine"
    }
  },
  "created_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "modified_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-managed-index-schema-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|202|Accepted|Schema recorded and queued|[ManagedIndexResponse](#schemamanagedindexresponse)|
|403|Forbidden|Permission denied|None|
|404|Not Found|Index not found|None|
|409|Conflict|Index is not ready, or another update won the race|None|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|The change cannot be applied to an existing index|None|
|503|Service Unavailable|Temporarily unavailable; retry later|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ApiKey
</aside>

## Search a managed index

<a id="opIdsearch_index_v1_context_search_indexes__index_name__search_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mistral.ai/v1/context/search-indexes/string/search \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "retriever": {
      "top_k": 20,
      "type": "keyword",
      "query": "string",
      "operator": "or",
      "filter": {
        "type": "and",
        "matches": [
          {}
        ]
      },
      "field": "string"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /v1/context/search-indexes/{index_name}/search`

Runs an approximate-nearest-neighbor vector search over the index and returns matching chunks, closest-first.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "retriever": {
    "top_k": 20,
    "type": "keyword",
    "query": "string",
    "operator": "or",
    "filter": {
      "type": "and",
      "matches": [
        {}
      ]
    },
    "field": "string"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="search-a-managed-index-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|index_name|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[SearchRequest](#schemasearchrequest)|true|none|
|» retriever|body|[KeywordRetriever](#schemakeywordretriever) \| [NearestNeighbourRetriever](#schemanearestneighbourretriever) \| [RRFRetriever](#schemarrfretriever)|true|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[KeywordRetriever](#schemakeywordretriever)|false|Retrieve document chunks with similar keywords to the given query.<br><br>Uses the default settings for the index on the field.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[NearestNeighbourRetriever](#schemanearestneighbourretriever)|false|Retrieve document chunks whose embeddings are closest to the query's.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[RRFRetriever](#schemarrfretriever)|false|Fuse child retriever rankings via reciprocal rank fusion.|

```json
{
  "hits": [

      "index_name": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

```json
    "name": "string"
  }
]
```

```json
    {
      "loc": [
        "string"
      ],
      "msg": "string",
      "type": "string",
      "input": null,
      "ctx": {}
    }
  ]
}
```

## Navigate to adjacent chunks

<a id="opIdnavigate_index_v1_context_search_indexes__index_name__navigate_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mistral.ai/v1/context/search-indexes/string/navigate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "source_id": "string",
    "start_offset": 0,
    "end_offset": 0,
    "direction": "next",
    "top_k": 1,
    "content_type": "content"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/context/search-indexes/{index_name}/navigate`

Returns the chunks adjacent to a position within a source, in reading order. NEXT fetches chunks at or after the end offset; PREVIOUS fetches chunks before the start offset. A 200 with an empty list means the source exists but no chunk falls in the requested direction; a 404 means the source has no chunks at all.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "source_id": "string",
  "start_offset": 0,
  "end_offset": 0,
  "direction": "next",
  "top_k": 1,
  "content_type": "content"
}
```

|» source_id|body|string|true|none|
|» start_offset|body|integer|true|none|
|» end_offset|body|integer|true|none|
|» direction|body|[NavigationDirection](#schemanavigationdirection)|true|none|
|» top_k|body|integer|false|none|
|» content_type|body|string|false|none|

|» direction|previous|

```json
}
```

## Grep for a pattern within a source

<a id="opIdgrep_index_v1_context_search_indexes__index_name__grep_post"></a>


`POST /v1/context/search-indexes/{index_name}/grep`

Lexical substring match within a single source, in reading order. A 200 with an empty list means the source exists but no chunk matched; a 404 means the source has no chunks at all.

```json
  "pattern": "string",
  "mode": "phrase",
  "top_k": 5,
  "content_type": "content"
```

## Generate a summary field for a managed index

<a id="opIdgenerate_managed_index_summary_post_v1_context_search_indexes__index_name__summary_field__language__post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mistral.ai/v1/context/search-indexes/string/summary_field/en \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /v1/context/search-indexes/{index_name}/summary_field/{language}`

Streams a summary for the managed index in chunks of json.

The first chunk contains metadata for the summary, the following contain
chunks of 'content' that should be joined together to form a full summary.

If force is true, regenerate the requested language even if a summary
already exists.

<h3 id="generate-a-summary-field-for-a-managed-index-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|language|path|string|true|none|
|index_name|path|string|true|none|
|force|query|boolean|false|Regenerate the summary even if one already exists for this language|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|language|en|
|language|fr|
|language|es|
|language|de|
|language|it|
|language|pt_br|
|language|pl|
|language|ar|
|language|nl|

> Example responses

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "detail": [
    {
      "loc": [
        "string"
      ],
      "msg": "string",
      "type": "string",
      "input": null,
      "ctx": {}
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="generate-a-summary-field-for-a-managed-index-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful Response|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Invalid request|None|
|403|Forbidden|Unauthorized|None|
|404|Not Found|Index not found|None|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation Error|[HTTPValidationError](#schemahttpvalidationerror)|
|500|Internal Server Error|Internal server error|None|
|503|Service Unavailable|Temporarily unavailable; retry later|None|

<h3 id="generate-a-summary-field-for-a-managed-index-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anyOf*|[SummaryMetadata](#schemasummarymetadata)|false|none|Summary content. Expected to be the first value returned.|
|*anyOf*|[SummaryChunk](#schemasummarychunk)|false|none|Regular content.|
|*anyOf*|[SummaryError](#schemasummaryerror)|false|none|If an error is encountered while streaming responses this is returned.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ApiKey
</aside>

`POST /v1/observability/datasets/{dataset_id}/imports/from-spans`

Starts an asynchronous import of the requested telemetry spans. References not returned by the tenant-scoped telemetry query are skipped without distinguishing absence from access restrictions.

## Search traces

<a id="opIdsearch_traces_v1_observability_traces_search_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mistral.ai/v1/observability/traces/search \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "search_expression": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/observability/traces/search`

Search traces

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "search_expression": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="search-traces-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|from|query|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|
|to|query|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|
|page_size|query|integer|false|none|
|cursor|query|string \| null|false|none|
|body|body|[TracesRequest](#schematracesrequest)|true|none|
|» search_expression|body|string \| null|false|Filter expression. Trace fields (e.g. `service_name`, `error_count`, `models_used`) are evaluated on the aggregated trace. Span attribute fields (e.g. `temporalWorkflowID`, `wf.type`, `gen_ai.provider.name`) are evaluated on the spans of the trace: a trace matches when one of its spans matches. Span attribute conditions combined with AND must hold on the same span, e.g. `temporalWorkflowID = 'wf-1' AND wf.type = 'activity'` only matches traces with a span carrying both attributes. Results are always one row per trace.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|

## CreatePrompt

<a id="opIdprompts_create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mistral.ai/v2/prompts \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "string",
    "definition": {
      "content": "string",
      "variables": [
        {
          "name": "string"
        }
      ]
    },
    "title": "string",
    "description": "string",
    "notes": "string",
    "sharingScope": "sharing_scope_unspecified",
    "aliases": [
      "string"
    ],
    "workspaceRelation": "share_relation_unspecified"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/prompts`

CreatePrompt

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "definition": {
    "content": "string",
    "variables": [
      {
        "name": "string"
      }
    ]
  },
  "title": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "notes": "string",
  "sharingScope": "sharing_scope_unspecified",
  "aliases": [
    "string"
  ],
  "workspaceRelation": "share_relation_unspecified"
}
```

<h3 id="createprompt-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreatePromptRequest](#schemacreatepromptrequest)|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|Stable object name.|
|» definition|body|[PromptDefinition](#schemapromptdefinition)|true|Versioned prompt content.|
|» title|body|string \| null|false|Display title.|
|» description|body|string \| null|false|Display description.|
|» notes|body|string \| null|false|Notes for this version.|
|» sharingScope|body|[RegistrySharingScope](#schemaregistrysharingscope)|false|Registry sharing scope.|
|» aliases|body|[string]|false|Aliases pointing to this version.|
|» workspaceRelation|body|[ShareRelation](#schemasharerelation)|false|Access every workspace member gets when sharing_scope is `workspace`. Defaults to `writer`, which is what a workspace publish granted before this field existed, so omitting it preserves today's behaviour exactly. Rejected unless sharing_scope is `workspace`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» sharingScope|sharing_scope_unspecified|
|» sharingScope|private|
|» sharingScope|workspace|
|» workspaceRelation|share_relation_unspecified|
|» workspaceRelation|reader|
|» workspaceRelation|writer|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
```

<h1 id="mistral-ai-api-betaserviceaccounts">beta.service_accounts</h1>

(beta) Service Accounts API.

## List Service Accounts

<a id="opIdlist_service_accounts_v1_service_accounts_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.mistral.ai/v1/service-accounts?offset=0&limit=1' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/service-accounts`

List the service accounts in a workspace, or across the organization.

Scoped to a workspace, this requires the Workspace admin (`workspace_admin`) role on
it. Omitting the workspace lists the whole organization and requires the Organization
admin (`organization_admin`) role instead.

``q`` narrows the list to accounts whose name or description contains it. ``order``
sorts by creation time (ascending by default).

<h3 id="list-service-accounts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace_id|query|string(uuid) \| null|false|none|
|include_deleted|query|boolean|false|none|
|q|query|string \| null|false|none|
|order|query|[SortOrder](#schemasortorder)|false|none|
|offset|query|integer|true|none|
|limit|query|integer|true|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|order|asc|
|order|desc|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
      "name": "string",
      "customer_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
      "organization_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
      "workspace_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
      "description": "string",
      "created_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "updated_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "deleted_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "detail": [
    {
      "loc": [
        "string"
      ],
      "msg": "string",
      "type": "string",
      "input": null,
      "ctx": {}
    }
  ]
}
```

## Create Trigger

<a id="opIdcreate_trigger_v1_triggers_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mistral.ai/v1/triggers \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "event_source_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "handler": "workflows",
    "action": {
      "primitive_id": "string",
      "type": "start_workflow"
    },
    "filters": "string",
    "owner_type": "workspace",
    "title": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/triggers`

Create Trigger

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "event_source_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "handler": "workflows",
  "action": {
    "primitive_id": "string",
    "type": "start_workflow"
  },
  "filters": "string",
  "owner_type": "workspace",
  "title": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-trigger-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreateTrigger](#schemacreatetrigger)|true|none|
|» event_source_id|body|string(uuid)|true|ID of the event source that fires this trigger|
|» handler|body|[TriggerHandler](#schematriggerhandler)|true|workflows, agents, or spaces|
|» action|body|[CreateTriggerAction](#schemacreatetriggeraction)|true|Action to execute when the trigger fires|
|» filters|body|string \| null|false|jmespath expression to filter events, e.g. event_type == 'push' && repository.name == 'dashboard'|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» owner_type|body|[TriggersOwnerType](#schematriggersownertype)|true|none|
|» title|body|string|true|Human-readable title of the trigger|

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» handler|workflows|
|» handler|agents|
|» handler|spaces|
|» owner_type|workspace|
|» owner_type|user|

reads only the user and never scopes by the active org.

## List Deployments

<a id="opIdlist_deployments_v1_workflows_deployments_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mistral.ai/v1/workflows/deployments \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/workflows/deployments`

List Deployments

<h3 id="list-deployments-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|active_only|query|boolean|false|none|
|is_hardened|query|boolean \| null|false|Filter deployments by hardened status|
|workflow_name|query|string \| null|false|none|
|created_by|query|string \| null|false|Filter deployments by creator's user id|
|owner|query|string \| null|false|Filter deployments by owner's user id|
|location_types|query|[[LocationType](#schemalocationtype)] \| null|false|Filter deployments with at least one worker on any of these location types (OR)|
|search|query|string \| null|false|Filter deployments by name or ID prefix|
|order_by|query|string \| null|false|Field to sort by. When omitted, active and managed deployments are grouped first, then sorted by created_at. When set, results are sorted purely by the specified field with no grouping.|
|order|query|string|false|Sort direction. Applied to order_by when set, or within each activity group when omitted.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Maximum number of deployments to return|
|cursor|query|string \| null|false|Cursor from a previous response for pagination|
|workspace_id|query|string(uuid) \| null|false|Workspace ID to scope the request to. Defaults to the caller's context.|
|repository_url|query|string \| null|false|Filter managed deployments by source repository URL (exact match)|
|dockerfile_path|query|string \| null|false|Filter managed deployments by Dockerfile path (exact match)|

|order|desc|

## Get Deployment Logs

<a id="opIdget_deployment_logs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mistral.ai/v1/workflows/deployments/string/logs \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/workflows/deployments/{name}/logs`

Retrieve logs for a deployment (across all of its workers).

Use `after`/`before`/`order` on the first request to set the time range and sort order; for
the next pages pass the `cursor` from the previous response (it remembers the range and order).

`log_type=build` serves the managed build pipeline's output instead. It pages the same way,
and a null `next_cursor` means the window is drained.

<h3 id="get-deployment-logs-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|string|true|none|
|log_type|query|[DeploymentLogType](#schemadeploymentlogtype)|false|Which stream to read. 'runtime' is the workers' own logs; 'build' reads the image build output and requires a managed deployment.|
|worker_name|query|string \| null|false|Filter logs by worker name|
|workflow_name|query|string \| null|false|Filter logs by workflow name|
|after|query|string(date-time) \| null|false|Only return logs at or after this timestamp|
|before|query|string(date-time) \| null|false|Only return logs before this timestamp|
|order|query|string|false|First-page sort order: 'asc' (oldest first) or 'desc'. Ignored when `cursor` is set.|
|cursor|query|string \| null|false|Pagination cursor from a previous response's `next_cursor`; carries the window and order|
|limit|query|integer|false|Maximum number of logs to return|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|log_type|build|
|log_type|runtime|
|order|asc|
|order|desc|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "results": [
    {
      "timestamp": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "trace_id": "string",
      "span_id": "string",
      "severity_text": "string",
      "body": "string",
      "log_attributes": {
        "property1": "string",
        "property2": "string"
      }
    }
  ],
  "next_cursor": "string"
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "detail": [
    {
      "loc": [
        "string"
      ],
      "msg": "string",
      "type": "string",
      "input": null,
      "ctx": {}
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="get-deployment-logs-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful Response|[DeploymentLogSearchResponse](#schemadeploymentlogsearchresponse)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation Error|[HTTPValidationError](#schemahttpvalidationerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ApiKey
</aside>

## Stream Deployment Logs

<a id="opIdstream_deployment_logs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mistral.ai/v1/workflows/deployments/string/logs/stream \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/workflows/deployments/{name}/logs/stream`

Stream logs for a deployment (all of its workers) via SSE.

Resume cursor comes from the `Last-Event-ID` header or `last_event_id` query param (header wins)
and takes precedence over `after`; omit all to tail from the deployment start.

<h3 id="stream-deployment-logs-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|string|true|none|
|worker_name|query|string \| null|false|Filter logs by worker name|
|workflow_name|query|string \| null|false|Filter logs by workflow name|
|after|query|string(date-time) \| null|false|Start a fresh stream at this timestamp (ignored when resuming via last_event_id)|
|last_event_id|query|string \| null|false|Resume from this cursor (a prior response's SSE id)|
|Last-Event-ID|header|string \| null|false|Resume from this cursor (a prior response's SSE id). Takes precedence over the query parameter.|

> Example responses

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "detail": [
    {
      "loc": [
        "string"
      ],
      "msg": "string",
      "type": "string",
      "input": null,
      "ctx": {}
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="stream-deployment-logs-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Stream of Server-Sent Events (SSE): `log` events carry a DeploymentLogRecord; `error` events carry a StreamError payload.|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Deployment not found|None|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation Error|[HTTPValidationError](#schemahttpvalidationerror)|
|503|Service Unavailable|Logs backend unavailable|None|

<h3 id="stream-deployment-logs-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|event|string|false|none|none|
|id|string|false|none|none|
|data|[DeploymentLogRecord](#schemadeploymentlogrecord) \| [StreamError](#schemastreamerror)|false|none|none|
|» *oneOf*|[DeploymentLogRecord](#schemadeploymentlogrecord)|false|none|none|
|» *oneOf*|[StreamError](#schemastreamerror)|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|event|log|
|event|error|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ApiKey
</aside>

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/workflows/executions/{execution_id}/logs`

Retrieve logs for a workflow execution.

Use `after`/`before`/`order` on the first request to set the time range and sort order; for
the next pages pass the `cursor` from the previous response (it remembers the range and order).

<h3 id="get-workflow-execution-logs-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|execution_id|path|string|true|none|
|run_id|query|string(uuid) \| null|false|Filter logs by workflow run ID|
|activity_id|query|string \| null|false|Filter logs by activity ID|
|after|query|string(date-time) \| null|false|Only return logs at or after this timestamp|
|before|query|string(date-time) \| null|false|Only return logs before this timestamp|
|order|query|string|false|First-page sort order: 'asc' (oldest first) or 'desc'. Ignored when `cursor` is set.|
|cursor|query|string \| null|false|Pagination cursor from a previous response's `next_cursor`; carries the window and order|
|limit|query|integer|false|Maximum number of logs to return|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|order|asc|
|order|desc|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "results": [
    {
      "timestamp": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "trace_id": "string",
      "span_id": "string",
      "severity_text": "string",
      "body": "string",
      "log_attributes": {
        "property1": "string",
        "property2": "string"
      }
    }
  ],
  "next_cursor": "string"
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "detail": [
    {
      "loc": [
        "string"
      ],
      "msg": "string",
      "type": "string",
      "input": null,
      "ctx": {}
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="get-workflow-execution-logs-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful Response|[ExecutionLogSearchResponse](#schemaexecutionlogsearchresponse)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation Error|[HTTPValidationError](#schemahttpvalidationerror)|

## Stream Workflow Execution Logs

<a id="opIdstream_workflow_execution_logs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mistral.ai/v1/workflows/executions/string/logs/stream \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/workflows/executions/{execution_id}/logs/stream`

Stream logs for a workflow execution via SSE.

Resume cursor comes from the `Last-Event-ID` header or `last_event_id` query param (header wins)
and takes precedence over `after`; omit all to tail from the execution start.

<h3 id="stream-workflow-execution-logs-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|execution_id|path|string|true|none|
|run_id|query|string(uuid) \| null|false|Filter logs by workflow run ID|
|activity_id|query|string \| null|false|Filter logs by activity ID|
|after|query|string(date-time) \| null|false|Start a fresh stream at this timestamp (ignored when resuming via last_event_id)|
|last_event_id|query|string \| null|false|Resume from this cursor (a prior response's SSE id)|
|Last-Event-ID|header|string \| null|false|Resume from this cursor (a prior response's SSE id). Takes precedence over the query parameter.|

> Example responses

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "detail": [
    {
      "loc": [
        "string"
      ],
      "msg": "string",
      "type": "string",
      "input": null,
      "ctx": {}
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="stream-workflow-execution-logs-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Stream of Server-Sent Events (SSE): `log` events carry an ExecutionLogRecord; `error` events carry a StreamError payload.|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Execution not found|None|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation Error|[HTTPValidationError](#schemahttpvalidationerror)|
|503|Service Unavailable|Logs backend unavailable|None|

<h3 id="stream-workflow-execution-logs-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|event|string|false|none|none|
|id|string|false|none|none|
|data|[ExecutionLogRecord](#schemaexecutionlogrecord) \| [StreamError](#schemastreamerror)|false|none|none|
|» *oneOf*|[ExecutionLogRecord](#schemaexecutionlogrecord)|false|none|none|
|» *oneOf*|[StreamError](#schemastreamerror)|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|event|log|
|event|error|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
