<h1 id="mistral-ai-api-workflowsmetrics">workflows.metrics</h1>

Workflows API - metrics.

## Get Workflow Metrics

<a id="opIdget_workflow_metrics_v1_workflows__workflow_name__metrics_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mistral.ai/v1/workflows/string/metrics \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/workflows/{workflow_name}/metrics`

Get comprehensive metrics for a specific workflow.

Args:
    workflow_name: The name of the workflow type to get metrics for
    start_time: Optional start time filter (ISO 8601 format)
    end_time: Optional end time filter (ISO 8601 format)

Returns:
    WorkflowMetrics: Dictionary containing metrics:
        - execution_count: Total number of executions
        - success_count: Number of successful executions
        - error_count: Number of failed/terminated executions
        - average_latency_ms: Average execution duration in milliseconds
        - retry_rate: Deprecated, always -1. Never measured retries; use error_count instead
        - latency_over_time: Time-series data of execution durations

Example:
    GET /v1/workflows/MyWorkflow/metrics
    GET /v1/workflows/MyWorkflow/metrics?start_time=2025-01-01T00:00:00Z
    GET /v1/workflows/MyWorkflow/metrics?start_time=2025-01-01T00:00:00Z&end_time=2025-12-31T23:59:59Z

<h3 id="get-workflow-metrics-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workflow_name|path|string|true|none|
|start_time|query|string(date-time) \| null|false|Filter workflows started after this time (ISO 8601)|
|end_time|query|string(date-time) \| null|false|Filter workflows started before this time (ISO 8601)|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "execution_count": {
    "value": 0
  },
  "success_count": {
    "value": 0
  },
  "error_count": {
    "value": 0
  },
  "average_latency_ms": {
    "value": 0
  },
  "latency_over_time": {
    "value": [
      [
        0,
        0
      ]
    ]
  },
  "retry_rate": {
    "value": 0
  }
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "detail": [
    {
      "loc": [
        "string"
      ],
      "msg": "string",
      "type": "string",
      "input": null,
      "ctx": {}
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="get-workflow-metrics-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful Response|[WorkflowMetrics](#schemaworkflowmetrics)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation Error|[HTTPValidationError](#schemahttpvalidationerror)|

<h1 id="mistral-ai-api-workflowsruns">workflows.runs</h1>

Workflows API - runs.

## List Runs

<a id="opIdlist_runs_v1_workflows_runs_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mistral.ai/v1/workflows/runs \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/workflows/runs`

List Runs

<h3 id="list-runs-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workflow_identifier|query|string \| null|false|Filter by workflow name or id|
|root_execution_id|query|string \| null|false|Filter by root execution id; returns the whole execution tree (the root and all its descendant sub-workflows).|
|search|query|string \| null|false|Search by workflow name, display name, or ID|
|status|query|[WorkflowExecutionStatus](#schemaworkflowexecutionstatus) \| [[WorkflowExecutionStatus](#schemaworkflowexecutionstatus)] \| null|false|Filter by workflow status|
|deployment_name|query|string \| null|false|Filter by deployment name|
|sort_by|query|string \| null|false|Field to sort by|
|order|query|string|false|Sort direction|
|start_time_after|query|string(date-time) \| null|false|Include runs with start_time >= value|
|start_time_before|query|string(date-time) \| null|false|Include runs with start_time &lt;= value|
|end_time_after|query|string(date-time) \| null|false|Include runs with end_time >= value. Running executions (no end_time) are excluded; use the status filter to include them.|
|end_time_before|query|string(date-time) \| null|false|Include runs with end_time &lt;= value. Running executions (no end_time) are excluded; use the status filter to include them.|
|user_id|query|string \| null|false|Filter by user id. Use 'current' to filter by the authenticated user|
|workflow_tags|query|[string] \| null|false|Filter to runs of workflows tagged with all listed tags (AND).|
|exclude_workflow_tags|query|[string] \| null|false|Exclude runs of workflows tagged with any of the listed tags.|
|include_internal|query|boolean|false|Include runs of internal/technical workflows (e.g. parallel-execution)|
|page_size|query|integer|false|Number of items per page|
|next_page_token|query|string \| null|false|Token for the next page of results|
|search_key|query|[string] \| null|false|Filter executions by search key as repeated entries (max 3, AND'd together). 'key:value' matches a similar value, 'key==:value' matches the exact value, a bare 'key' matches executions that have the key set at all, and 'key==' matches executions whose value for the key is null.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|order|asc|
|order|desc|

|workspaceRelation|[ShareRelation](#schemasharerelation)|false|none|Access every workspace member gets when sharing_scope is `workspace`. Defaults to `writer`, which is what a workspace publish granted before this field existed, so omitting it preserves today's behaviour exactly. Rejected unless sharing_scope is `workspace`.|

<h2 id="tocS_IPAPhoneme">IPAPhoneme</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaipaphoneme"></a>
<a id="schema_IPAPhoneme"></a>
<a id="tocSipaphoneme"></a>
<a id="tocsipaphoneme"></a>

```json
"a"
```

The IPA phone inventory usable in pronunciation hints.

``StrEnum`` members' values are their (lowercase) names via ``auto()``, so each member IS
the IPA string it represents. Using an enum makes ``phoneme_hints`` values self-validating
at the API boundary (pydantic rejects any phone outside this set). **Append-only**: never
reorder or remove entries, only add new phones (e.g. for future languages) at the end.

<h2 id="tocS_ResponseFormat">ResponseFormat</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaresponseformat"></a>
<a id="schema_ResponseFormat"></a>
<a id="tocSresponseformat"></a>
<a id="tocsresponseformat"></a>

```json
{
  "type": "text"
}
```

Specify the format that the model must output. By default it will use `{ "type": "text" }`. Setting to `{ "type": "json_object" }` enables JSON mode, which guarantees the message the model generates is in JSON. When using JSON mode you MUST also instruct the model to produce JSON yourself with a system or a user message. Setting to `{ "type": "json_schema" }` enables JSON schema mode, which guarantees the message the model generates is in JSON and follows the schema you provide. Note: on third-party models (for example GLM), the schema is still enforced, but field descriptions may not influence the output; put field-level requirements in the prompt.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|[ResponseFormats](#schemaresponseformats)|false|none|none|
|json_schema|[JsonSchema](#schemajsonschema) \| null|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|text|
|type|json_object|
|type|json_schema|

<h2 id="tocS_ChatCompletionRequest">ChatCompletionRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemachatcompletionrequest"></a>
<a id="schema_ChatCompletionRequest"></a>
<a id="tocSchatcompletionrequest"></a>
<a id="tocschatcompletionrequest"></a>

```json
{
  "model": "mistral-large-latest",
  "temperature": 0,
  "top_p": 0.1,
  "max_tokens": 0,
  "stream": false,
  "stop": "string",
  "random_seed": 0,
  "metadata": {},
  "messages": [
    {
      "role": "user",
      "content": "Who is the best French painter? Answer in one short sentence."
    }
  ],
  "response_format": {
    "type": "text"
  },
  "tools": [
    {
      "type": "function",
      "function": {
        "name": "string",
        "description": "",
        "strict": false,
        "parameters": {}
      }
    }
  ],
  "tool_choice": "auto",
  "presence_penalty": -2,
  "frequency_penalty": -2,
  "min_tokens": 0,
  "repetition_penalty": 0.1,
  "top_k": -1,
  "logprobs": true,
  "top_logprobs": 0,
  "prompt_logprobs": true,
  "top_prompt_logprobs": 0,
  "n": 1,
  "prediction": {
    "type": "content",
    "content": ""
  },
  "parallel_tool_calls": true,
  "reasoning_effort": "none",
  "prompt_mode": "reasoning",
  "guardrails": [
    {
      "block_on_error": false,
      "moderation_llm_v1": {
        "model_name": "mistral-moderation-2411",
        "custom_category_thresholds": {
          "sexual": 0,
          "hate_and_discrimination": 0,
          "violence_and_threats": 0,
          "dangerous_and_criminal_content": 0,
          "selfharm": 0,
          "health": 0,
          "financial": 0,
          "law": 0,
          "pii": 0
        },
        "ignore_other_categories": false,
        "action": "none"
      },
      "moderation_llm_v2": {
        "model_name": "mistral-moderation-2603",
        "custom_category_thresholds": {
          "sexual": 0,
          "hate_and_discrimination": 0,
          "violence_and_threats": 0,
          "dangerous": 0,
          "criminal": 0,
          "selfharm": 0,
          "health": 0,
          "financial": 0,
          "law": 0,
          "pii": 0,
          "jailbreaking": 0
        },
        "ignore_other_categories": false,
        "action": "none"
      }
    }
  ],
  "prompt_cache_key": "string",
  "service_tier": "auto",
  "safe_prompt": false
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|model|string|true|none|ID of the model to use. You can use the [List Available Models](/api/#tag/models/operation/list_models_v1_models_get) API to see all of your available models, or see our [Model overview](/models) for model descriptions.|
|temperature|number \| null|false|none|What sampling temperature to use, we recommend between 0.0 and 0.7. Higher values like 0.7 will make the output more random, while lower values like 0.2 will make it more focused and deterministic. We generally recommend altering this or `top_p` but not both. The default value varies depending on the model you are targeting. Call the `/models` endpoint to retrieve the appropriate value.|
|top_p|number \| null|false|none|Nucleus sampling, where the model considers the results of the tokens with `top_p` probability mass. So 0.1 means only the tokens comprising the top 10% probability mass are considered. We generally recommend altering this or `temperature` but not both.|
|max_tokens|integer \| null|false|none|The maximum number of tokens to generate in the completion. The token count of your prompt plus `max_tokens` cannot exceed the model's context length.|
|stream|boolean|false|none|Whether to stream back partial progress. If set, tokens will be sent as data-only server-side events as they become available, with the stream terminated by a data: [DONE] message. Otherwise, the server will hold the request open until the timeout or until completion, with the response containing the full result as JSON.|
|stop|string \| [string] \| null|false|none|Stop generation if this token is detected. Or if one of these tokens is detected when providing an array|
|random_seed|integer \| null|false|none|The seed to use for random sampling. If set, different calls will generate deterministic results.|
|metadata|object \| null|false|none|none|
|messages|[[SystemMessage](#schemasystemmessage) \| [UserMessage](#schemausermessage) \| [AssistantMessage](#schemaassistantmessage) \| [ToolMessage](#schematoolmessage)]|true|none|The prompt(s) to generate completions for, encoded as a list of dict with role and content.|
|response_format|[ResponseFormat](#schemaresponseformat)|false|none|Specify the format that the model must output. By default it will use `{ "type": "text" }`. Setting to `{ "type": "json_object" }` enables JSON mode, which guarantees the message the model generates is in JSON. When using JSON mode you MUST also instruct the model to produce JSON yourself with a system or a user message. Setting to `{ "type": "json_schema" }` enables JSON schema mode, which guarantees the message the model generates is in JSON and follows the schema you provide. Note: on third-party models (for example GLM), the schema is still enforced, but field descriptions may not influence the output; put field-level requirements in the prompt.|
|tools|[[Tool](#schematool) \| [ImageGenerationTool](#schemaimagegenerationtool) \| [DocumentLibraryTool](#schemadocumentlibrarytool) \| [CustomConnector](#schemacustomconnector)] \| null|false|none|A list of tools the model may call. Use this to provide a list of functions the model may generate JSON inputs for.|
|tool_choice|[ToolChoiceEnum](#schematoolchoiceenum) \| [NamedToolChoice](#schemanamedtoolchoice)|false|none|Controls which (if any) tool is called by the model. `none` means the model will not call any tool and instead generates a message. `auto` means the model can pick between generating a message or calling one or more tools. `any` or `required` means the model must call one or more tools. Specifying a particular tool via `{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "my_function"}}` forces the model to call that tool.|
|presence_penalty|number \| null|false|none|The `presence_penalty` determines how much the model penalizes the repetition of words or phrases. A higher presence penalty encourages the model to use a wider variety of words and phrases, making the output more diverse and creative.|
|frequency_penalty|number \| null|false|none|The `frequency_penalty` penalizes the repetition of words based on their frequency in the generated text. A higher frequency penalty discourages the model from repeating words that have already appeared frequently in the output, promoting diversity and reducing repetition.|
|min_tokens|integer \| null|false|none|none|
|repetition_penalty|number \| null|false|none|none|
|top_k|integer \| null|false|none|none|
|logprobs|boolean \| null|false|none|none|
|top_logprobs|integer \| null|false|none|none|
|prompt_logprobs|boolean \| null|false|none|none|
|top_prompt_logprobs|integer \| null|false|none|none|
|n|integer \| null|false|none|Number of completions to return for each request, input tokens are only billed once.|
|prediction|[Prediction](#schemaprediction)|false|none|**Deprecated.** Deprecated: the API accepts this field but ignores it, and it will be removed in a future major version.|
|parallel_tool_calls|boolean|false|none|Whether to enable parallel function calling during tool use, when enabled the model can call multiple tools in parallel.|
|reasoning_effort|[ReasoningEffort](#schemareasoningeffort) \| null|false|none|none|
|prompt_mode|[MistralPromptMode](#schemamistralpromptmode) \| null|false|none|Allows toggling between the reasoning mode and no system prompt. When set to `reasoning` the system prompt for reasoning models will be used.|
|guardrails|[[GuardrailConfig](#schemaguardrailconfig)] \| null|false|none|none|
|prompt_cache_key|string \| null|false|none|none|
|service_tier|[RequestedServiceTier](#schemarequestedservicetier) \| null|false|none|Determines whether to serve the request using priority or standard capacity.|
|safe_prompt|boolean|false|none|Whether to inject a safety prompt before all conversations.|

Per-block confidence scores, computed per-word from model logprobs.

All fields ``None`` when the block couldn't be scored.
Individual fields ``None`` when that signal is absent — e.g. an image-only block has
no caption, so content scores are ``None``.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|average_content_confidence_score|number \| null|false|none|Average confidence over the block's content (caption) tokens. None when the block has no textual content (e.g. image-only entry).|
|minimum_content_confidence_score|number \| null|false|none|Minimum per-word content confidence in the block. None when the block has no textual content.|
|block_type_confidence_score|number \| null|false|none|Confidence in the block type (e.g. 'text', 'title', 'table'). None when the entry had no block type or the block type span could not be located.|

<h2 id="tocS_OCRPageConfidenceScores">OCRPageConfidenceScores</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaocrpageconfidencescores"></a>
<a id="schema_OCRPageConfidenceScores"></a>
<a id="tocSocrpageconfidencescores"></a>
<a id="tocsocrpageconfidencescores"></a>

```json
{
  "word_confidence_scores": [
    {
      "text": "string",
      "confidence": 0,
      "start_index": 0
    }
  ],
  "average_page_confidence_score": 0,
  "minimum_page_confidence_score": 0
}
```

Confidence scores for an OCR page at various granularities.

Note on page-level stats:
- For 'page' and 'block' granularity: average/minimum are computed from per-token
  exp(logprob). Neither ``word_confidence_scores`` nor ``token_scores`` is populated.
  Per-block scores are attached to response blocks separately for 'block' granularity.
- For 'word' granularity: average/minimum are computed from per-word confidence, where
  each word's confidence is exp(mean(token_logprobs)) — a geometric mean over the
  word's subword tokens. ``word_confidence_scores`` is populated.
- For 'token' granularity (internal): average/minimum are computed from
  ``token_scores``; ``token_scores`` is populated.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|word_confidence_scores|[[OCRConfidenceScore](#schemaocrconfidencescore)]|false|none|Word-level confidence scores (populated only for 'word' granularity)|
|average_page_confidence_score|number|true|none|Average confidence score for the page|
|minimum_page_confidence_score|number|true|none|Minimum confidence score for the page|

```json
{
```

```json
    "type": "file",
    "file_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
  },
  "pages": "string",
  "include_image_base64": true,
  "image_limit": 0,
  "image_min_size": 0,
  "bbox_annotation_format": {
    "type": "text"
  },
  "document_annotation_format": {
    "type": "text"
  },
  "document_annotation_prompt": "string",
  "table_format": "markdown",
  "extract_header": false,
  "extract_footer": false,
  "include_blocks": true,
  "confidence_scores_granularity": "word"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|model|string \| null|true|none|none|
|document|[FileChunk](#schemafilechunk) \| [DocumentURLChunk](#schemadocumenturlchunk) \| [ImageURLChunk](#schemaimageurlchunk)|true|none|Document to run OCR on|
|pages|string \| [integer] \| null|false|none|Specific pages to process. Accepts a list of integers or a string of comma-separated numbers and ranges (e.g. '0,1,2' or '0-5' or '0,2-4'). Page numbers start from 0.|
|include_image_base64|boolean \| null|false|none|Include image URLs in response|
|image_limit|integer \| null|false|none|Max images to extract|
|image_min_size|integer \| null|false|none|Minimum height and width of image to extract|
|bbox_annotation_format|[ResponseFormat](#schemaresponseformat) \| null|false|none|Structured output class for extracting useful information from each extracted bounding box / image from document. Only json_schema is valid for this field|
|document_annotation_format|[ResponseFormat](#schemaresponseformat) \| null|false|none|Structured output class for extracting useful information from the entire document. Only json_schema is valid for this field|
|document_annotation_prompt|string \| null|false|none|Optional prompt to guide the model in extracting structured output from the entire document. A document_annotation_format must be provided.|
|table_format|string \| null|false|none|none|
|extract_header|boolean|false|none|Extract the page header into the response's `header` field and remove it from the markdown content|
|extract_footer|boolean|false|none|Extract the page footer into the response's `footer` field and remove it from the markdown content|
|include_blocks|boolean|false|none|Return paragraph-level bounding boxes for all content blocks in the response|
|confidence_scores_granularity|string \| null|false|none|Granularity for confidence scores: 'page' (aggregate only), 'word' (per-word scores), or 'block' (per-block scores). Defaults to None (no confidence scores) to keep response payload small.|

<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemafile"></a>
<a id="schema_File"></a>
<a id="tocSfile"></a>
<a id="tocsfile"></a>

```json
"string"
```

The File object (not file name) to be uploaded.
 To upload a file and specify a custom file name you should format your request as such:
 ```bash
 file=@path/to/your/file.jsonl;filename=custom_name.jsonl
 ```
 Otherwise, you can just keep the original file name:
 ```bash
 file=@path/to/your/file.jsonl
 ```

```json
{
```

```json
    "type": "content",
    "content": ""
  },
  "parallel_tool_calls": true,
  "reasoning_effort": "none",
  "prompt_mode": "reasoning",
  "guardrails": [
    {
      "block_on_error": false,
      "moderation_llm_v1": {
        "model_name": "mistral-moderation-2411",
        "custom_category_thresholds": {
          "sexual": 0,
          "hate_and_discrimination": 0,
          "violence_and_threats": 0,
          "dangerous_and_criminal_content": 0,
          "selfharm": 0,
          "health": 0,
          "financial": 0,
          "law": 0,
          "pii": 0
        },
        "ignore_other_categories": false,
        "action": "none"
      },
      "moderation_llm_v2": {
        "model_name": "mistral-moderation-2603",
        "custom_category_thresholds": {
          "sexual": 0,
          "hate_and_discrimination": 0,
          "violence_and_threats": 0,
          "dangerous": 0,
          "criminal": 0,
          "selfharm": 0,
          "health": 0,
          "financial": 0,
          "law": 0,
          "pii": 0,
          "jailbreaking": 0
        },
        "ignore_other_categories": false,
        "action": "none"
      }
    }
  ],
  "prompt_cache_key": "string",
  "service_tier": "auto",
  "agent_id": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|max_tokens|integer \| null|false|none|The maximum number of tokens to generate in the completion. The token count of your prompt plus `max_tokens` cannot exceed the model's context length.|
|stream|boolean|false|none|Whether to stream back partial progress. If set, tokens will be sent as data-only server-side events as they become available, with the stream terminated by a data: [DONE] message. Otherwise, the server will hold the request open until the timeout or until completion, with the response containing the full result as JSON.|
|stop|string \| [string] \| null|false|none|Stop generation if this token is detected. Or if one of these tokens is detected when providing an array|
|random_seed|integer \| null|false|none|The seed to use for random sampling. If set, different calls will generate deterministic results.|
|metadata|object \| null|false|none|none|
|messages|[[SystemMessage](#schemasystemmessage) \| [UserMessage](#schemausermessage) \| [AssistantMessage](#schemaassistantmessage) \| [ToolMessage](#schematoolmessage)]|true|none|The prompt(s) to generate completions for, encoded as a list of dict with role and content.|
|response_format|[ResponseFormat](#schemaresponseformat)|false|none|Specify the format that the model must output. By default it will use `{ "type": "text" }`. Setting to `{ "type": "json_object" }` enables JSON mode, which guarantees the message the model generates is in JSON. When using JSON mode you MUST also instruct the model to produce JSON yourself with a system or a user message. Setting to `{ "type": "json_schema" }` enables JSON schema mode, which guarantees the message the model generates is in JSON and follows the schema you provide. Note: on third-party models (for example GLM), the schema is still enforced, but field descriptions may not influence the output; put field-level requirements in the prompt.|
|tools|[[Tool](#schematool) \| [ImageGenerationTool](#schemaimagegenerationtool) \| [DocumentLibraryTool](#schemadocumentlibrarytool) \| [CustomConnector](#schemacustomconnector)] \| null|false|none|none|
|tool_choice|[ToolChoiceEnum](#schematoolchoiceenum) \| [NamedToolChoice](#schemanamedtoolchoice)|false|none|none|
|presence_penalty|number \| null|false|none|The `presence_penalty` determines how much the model penalizes the repetition of words or phrases. A higher presence penalty encourages the model to use a wider variety of words and phrases, making the output more diverse and creative.|
|frequency_penalty|number \| null|false|none|The `frequency_penalty` penalizes the repetition of words based on their frequency in the generated text. A higher frequency penalty discourages the model from repeating words that have already appeared frequently in the output, promoting diversity and reducing repetition.|
|min_tokens|integer \| null|false|none|none|
|repetition_penalty|number \| null|false|none|none|
|top_k|integer \| null|false|none|none|
|logprobs|boolean \| null|false|none|none|
|top_logprobs|integer \| null|false|none|none|
|prompt_logprobs|boolean \| null|false|none|none|
|top_prompt_logprobs|integer \| null|false|none|none|
|n|integer \| null|false|none|Number of completions to return for each request, input tokens are only billed once.|
|prediction|[Prediction](#schemaprediction)|false|none|**Deprecated.** Deprecated: the API accepts this field but ignores it, and it will be removed in a future major version.|
|parallel_tool_calls|boolean|false|none|none|
|reasoning_effort|[ReasoningEffort](#schemareasoningeffort) \| null|false|none|none|
|prompt_mode|[MistralPromptMode](#schemamistralpromptmode) \| null|false|none|Allows toggling between the reasoning mode and no system prompt. When set to `reasoning` the system prompt for reasoning models will be used.|
|guardrails|[[GuardrailConfig](#schemaguardrailconfig)] \| null|false|none|none|
|prompt_cache_key|string \| null|false|none|none|
|service_tier|[RequestedServiceTier](#schemarequestedservicetier) \| null|false|none|Determines whether to serve the request using priority or standard capacity.|
|agent_id|string|true|none|The ID of the agent to use for this completion.|

<h2 id="tocS_ClassificationStatisticSpec">ClassificationStatisticSpec</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaclassificationstatisticspec"></a>
<a id="schema_ClassificationStatisticSpec"></a>
<a id="tocSclassificationstatisticspec"></a>
<a id="tocsclassificationstatisticspec"></a>

```json
{
  "kind": "precision",
  "positive_label": "string",
  "average": "macro",
  "expected_key": "expected",
  "labels": [
    "string"
  ],
  "goal": {
    "operator": "string",
    "value": null,
    "min": 0,
    "max": 0,
    "values": [
      null
    ],
    "metric": "string"
  }
}
```

A classification metric (``precision``/``recall``/``f1``) over ``(expected, predicted)`` pairs.

The predicted label is the score ``value``; the expected label is read from the score ``metadata``
under ``expected_key`` (default ``"expected"``). Provide **exactly one** of ``positive_label`` (a
binary metric scored against that one class) or ``average`` (a multi-class averaging scheme).

``labels`` pins the class universe so filtered views keep a stable, comparable denominator.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|kind|string|true|none|none|
|positive_label|string \| null|false|none|none|
|average|string \| null|false|none|none|
|expected_key|string|false|none|none|
|labels|[string] \| null|false|none|none|
|goal|[GoalSpec](#schemagoalspec) \| null|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|kind|precision|
|kind|recall|
|kind|f1|

<h2 id="tocS_ConfusionMatrix">ConfusionMatrix</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaconfusionmatrix"></a>
<a id="schema_ConfusionMatrix"></a>
<a id="tocSconfusionmatrix"></a>
<a id="tocsconfusionmatrix"></a>

```json
{
  "labels": [
    "string"
  ],
  "matrix": [
    [
      0
    ]
  ]
}
```

A confusion matrix over ``(expected, predicted)`` label pairs.

``matrix[i][j]`` is the number of samples whose expected label is ``labels[i]`` and predicted
label is ``labels[j]``. It is the complete, aggregatable representation: precision/recall/f1 for
any class derive from it, and matrices from several runs merge by element-wise sum.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|labels|[string]|true|none|none|
|matrix|[[integer]]|true|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_DisplaySpec">DisplaySpec</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadisplayspec"></a>
<a id="schema_DisplaySpec"></a>
<a id="tocSdisplayspec"></a>
<a id="tocsdisplayspec"></a>

```json
{
  "format": "number",
  "unit": "string",
  "decimals": 0,
  "metric": "string"
}
```

How the UI renders an evaluator's numeric values (scores, score-scale statistics, goal thresholds).

Display only: stored values and computed statistics never change. ``percent`` reads the value as a
fraction (0.63 renders as 63%), ``integer`` rounds it, ``number`` renders ``decimals`` decimals.
``unit`` is a free suffix ("s", "ms", "chars"), not allowed with ``percent`` (its ``%`` is the unit).
All fields unset = the default rendering.

``metric`` (run evaluators only) names the run evaluator metric this format applies to. Without it, the
spec formats the main value and is the default format of every metric.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|format|[DisplayFormat](#schemadisplayformat) \| null|false|none|none|
|unit|string \| null|false|none|none|
|decimals|integer \| null|false|none|none|
|metric|string \| null|false|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_RunOwnershipFilter">RunOwnershipFilter</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemarunownershipfilter"></a>
<a id="schema_RunOwnershipFilter"></a>
<a id="tocSrunownershipfilter"></a>
<a id="tocsrunownershipfilter"></a>

```json
{
  "combinator": "and",
  "creator_ids": [],
  "project_ids": [],
  "starred_by_me": false
}
```

OR-able group isolating the "runs I care about" default (created by me OR in my starred projects).

Kept separate from the plain generic filters so it can OR internally while still AND-ing with
everything else. The UI drives it via two sugar chips: "Created by me" writes `creator_ids`, and
"Starred projects" sets `starred_by_me`. Dropping a chip clears its term and the OR collapses to the
remaining one; dropping both leaves the group empty (no ownership scoping).

`starred_by_me` is resolved server-side against the caller's favorites, so the client never has to
page through projects to collect starred ids — and a caller with zero starred projects correctly
matches no runs (rather than falling through to the whole workspace). `project_ids` remains for
explicit, caller-supplied project scoping.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|combinator|[FilterCombinator](#schemafiltercombinator)|false|none|none|
|creator_ids|[string(uuid)]|false|none|none|
|project_ids|[string(uuid)]|false|none|none|
|starred_by_me|boolean|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|combinator|and|
|combinator|or|

<h2 id="tocS_ScalarStatisticValue">ScalarStatisticValue</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemascalarstatisticvalue"></a>
<a id="schema_ScalarStatisticValue"></a>
<a id="tocSscalarstatisticvalue"></a>
<a id="tocsscalarstatisticvalue"></a>

```json
{
  "type": "scalar",
  "id": "string",
  "value": 0,
  "sample_count": 0
}
```

A single scalar computed run-level statistic: its canonical id and numeric value.

``value`` is ``None`` when the statistic is not evaluable (e.g. a ``sum`` or percentile over an
empty numeric sample). A declared ``count`` is always evaluable and is ``0`` on an empty sample.

The ``type`` discriminator lets future result shapes (e.g. a categorical ``categories`` or a
``distribution``) join a union without overloading this model; consumers dispatch on ``type``.

### Properties

|type|string|false|none|none|
|id|string|true|none|none|
|value|number \| null|false|none|none|
|sample_count|integer \| null|false|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_SimpleNumericStatisticSpec">SimpleNumericStatisticSpec</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemasimplenumericstatisticspec"></a>
<a id="schema_SimpleNumericStatisticSpec"></a>
<a id="tocSsimplenumericstatisticspec"></a>
<a id="tocssimplenumericstatisticspec"></a>

```json
{
  "kind": "avg",
  "weight_key": "string",
  "goal": {
    "operator": "string",
    "value": null,
    "min": 0,
    "max": 0,
    "values": [
      null
    ],
    "metric": "string"
  }
}
```

A scalar numeric reduction (``avg``/``sum``/``min``/``max``/``std``/``count``).

``weight_key`` (``avg`` only) turns the mean into a weighted mean, ``sum(w * x) / sum(w)``, where
each score's weight ``w`` is read from its ``metadata`` under that key. Scores whose weight is
missing, non-numeric or negative are left out of that statistic.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|kind|string|true|none|none|
|weight_key|string \| null|false|none|none|
|goal|[GoalSpec](#schemagoalspec) \| null|false|none|none|

|kind|sum|
|kind|min|

|kind|count|

```json
      }
    }
  ]
```

Mapping rules applied independently to every requested telemetry span.

Version 1 mappings are optional per span: a missing, null, blank-string, or empty-array
source omits the target key. JSON object and array strings become structured values;
scalar-looking and malformed JSON strings remain strings.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|true|none|Name of the credentials. Use this name to access or modify your credentials.|
|title|string \| null|false|none|Human-readable title for the credentials.|
|is_default|boolean \| null|false|none|Controls whether this credential is the default for its auth method. On creation: if no credential exists yet for this auth method, the credential is automatically set as default when is_default is true or omitted; setting is_default to false is rejected because a default must exist. If other credentials already exist, setting is_default to true promotes this credential (demoting the previous default); false or omitted creates it as non-default. On update: true promotes this credential, false is rejected if it is currently the default (promote another credential first), omitted leaves the default status unchanged.|
|credentials|[ConnectionCredentialsInput](#schemaconnectioncredentialsinput) \| null|false|none|The credential data (headers, query_params, bearer_token, or OAuth2 client credentials).|

<h2 id="tocS_HTTPStatus">HTTPStatus</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemahttpstatus"></a>
<a id="schema_HTTPStatus"></a>
<a id="tocShttpstatus"></a>
<a id="tocshttpstatus"></a>

```json
100
```

HTTP status codes and reason phrases

Status codes from the following RFCs are all observed:

    * RFC 7231: Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP/1.1), obsoletes 2616
    * RFC 6585: Additional HTTP Status Codes
    * RFC 3229: Delta encoding in HTTP
    * RFC 4918: HTTP Extensions for WebDAV, obsoletes 2518
    * RFC 5842: Binding Extensions to WebDAV
    * RFC 7238: Permanent Redirect
    * RFC 2295: Transparent Content Negotiation in HTTP
    * RFC 2774: An HTTP Extension Framework
    * RFC 7725: An HTTP Status Code to Report Legal Obstacles
    * RFC 7540: Hypertext Transfer Protocol Version 2 (HTTP/2)
    * RFC 2324: Hyper Text Coffee Pot Control Protocol (HTCPCP/1.0)
    * RFC 8297: An HTTP Status Code for Indicating Hints
    * RFC 8470: Using Early Data in HTTP

Which log stream a deployment's logs come from.

`runtime` is what the workers themselves emit. `build` only exists for managed
deployments: it is the image build pipeline's output, which no worker reports.

|repository_url|string \| null|false|none|Repository to build the worker from, set instead of 'archive_id': a GitHub repository (`https://github.com/&lt;owner&gt;/&lt;repo&gt;`) or a repository on the Mistral git server (`https://api.globalaegis.net/v1/git/&lt;workspace&gt;/&lt;repo&gt;.git`). |revision|string \| null|false|none|none|
|archive_id|string(uuid) \| null|false|none|Mistral Cloud archive to build the worker from instead of a repository. The archive is the whole build context: 'dockerfile_path' is relative to its root, and 'build_directory' must be unset.|
|backend_spec|[DeploymentMistralCloudBackendSpec](#schemadeploymentmistralcloudbackendspec) \| null|false|none|Backend-specific configuration for the Mistral Cloud backend.|
|requested_roles|[string] \| null|false|none|Workspace roles, by name, that the deployment's service account holds beyond `workflow_executor`. Granted only if the deploying user holds them.|

Wrapper for encrypted patch values in selective json_patch encryption.

When partial encryption mode is enabled and a patch targets an EncryptedStrField,

The type field acts as a discriminator to distinguish this from user data.

Schedule definition for partial updates.

All fields are optional (inherited from _ScheduleRequestBase). Only explicitly-set
fields are applied during an update; unset fields preserve the existing schedule values.

|intervals|[[ScheduleInterval](#schemascheduleinterval)]|false|none|Interval-based specification of times.|
|cron_expressions|[string]|false|none|Cron-based specification of times.|
|skip|[[ScheduleCalendar](#schemaschedulecalendar)]|false|none|Set of calendar times to skip.|
|start_at|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|Time after which the first action may be run.|
|end_at|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|Time after which no more actions will be run.|
|jitter|string(duration) \| null|false|none|Jitter to apply each action.<br><br>An action's scheduled time will be incremented by a random value between 0<br>and this value if present (but not past the next schedule).<br>|
|time_zone_name|string \| null|false|none|IANA time zone name, for example ``US/Central``.|
|policy|[SchedulePolicy](#schemaschedulepolicy)|false|none|Policy for the schedule.|
|max_executions|integer \| null|false|none|Maximum number of times this schedule will trigger a workflow execution. Once this limit is reached, no further executions are triggered automatically. null means unlimited.|

Specification of the times scheduled actions may occur.

The times are the union of :py:attr:`calendars`, :py:attr:`intervals`, and
:py:attr:`cron_expressions` excluding anything in :py:attr:`skip`.

Used for input where schedule_id is optional (can be provided or auto-generated).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|input|object|true|none|Input to provide to the workflow when starting it.|
|calendars|[[ScheduleCalendar](#schemaschedulecalendar)]|false|none|Calendar-based specification of times.|
|intervals|[[ScheduleInterval](#schemascheduleinterval)]|false|none|Interval-based specification of times.|
|cron_expressions|[string]|false|none|Cron-based specification of times.|
|skip|[[ScheduleCalendar](#schemaschedulecalendar)]|false|none|Set of calendar times to skip.|
|start_at|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|Time after which the first action may be run.|
|end_at|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|Time after which no more actions will be run.|
|jitter|string(duration) \| null|false|none|Jitter to apply each action.<br><br>An action's scheduled time will be incremented by a random value between 0<br>and this value if present (but not past the next schedule).<br>|
|time_zone_name|string \| null|false|none|IANA time zone name, for example ``US/Central``.|
|policy|[SchedulePolicy](#schemaschedulepolicy)|false|none|Policy for the schedule.|
|max_executions|integer \| null|false|none|Maximum number of times this schedule will trigger a workflow execution. Once this limit is reached, no further executions are triggered automatically. null means unlimited.|
|schedule_id|string \| null|false|none|Unique identifier for the schedule.|

Output representation of a schedule with required schedule_id.

Used when returning schedules from the API where schedule_id is always present.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|input|object|true|none|Input to provide to the workflow when starting it.|
|calendars|[[ScheduleCalendar](#schemaschedulecalendar)]|false|none|Calendar-based specification of times.|
|intervals|[[ScheduleInterval](#schemascheduleinterval)]|false|none|Interval-based specification of times.|
|cron_expressions|[string]|false|none|Cron-based specification of times.|
|skip|[[ScheduleCalendar](#schemaschedulecalendar)]|false|none|Set of calendar times to skip.|
|start_at|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|Time after which the first action may be run.|
|end_at|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|Time after which no more actions will be run.|
|jitter|string(duration) \| null|false|none|Jitter to apply each action.<br><br>An action's scheduled time will be incremented by a random value between 0<br>and this value if present (but not past the next schedule).<br>|
|time_zone_name|string \| null|false|none|IANA time zone name, for example ``US/Central``.|
|policy|[SchedulePolicy](#schemaschedulepolicy)|false|none|Policy for the schedule.|
|schedule_id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the schedule.|
|remaining_executions|integer \| null|false|none|Remaining workflow executions before this schedule stops triggering automatically. null means unlimited; 0 means the limit has been reached and the schedule is exhausted.|
|workflow_name|string|true|none|Name of the workflow this schedule triggers.|
|deployment_name|string \| null|false|none|Name of the deployment this schedule targets.|
|user_id|string \| null|false|none|ID of the user who created the schedule.|
|paused|boolean|true|none|Whether the schedule is currently paused.|
|note|string \| null|false|none|Human-readable note associated with the current pause or resume state.|
|future_executions|[[ScheduleFutureExecution](#schemaschedulefutureexecution)]|false|none|Upcoming scheduled executions (10 next executions, earliest first).|
|recent_executions|[[ScheduleRecentExecution](#schemaschedulerecentexecution)]|false|none|Most recent scheduled executions (10 most recent, newest last).|

Trace response in OpenTelemetry format.

This is the unified trace format used across all trace providers (Tempo, ClickHouse, etc.).
Regardless of the underlying backend, all trace data is normalized to this Tempo-compatible
OpenTelemetry format to ensure consistency in the API response structure.

Emitted when a workflow execution is canceled.

This is a terminal event indicating the workflow was explicitly canceled.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|event_id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for this event instance.|
|event_timestamp|integer|true|none|Unix timestamp in nanoseconds when the event was created.|
|root_workflow_exec_id|string|true|none|Execution ID of the root workflow that initiated this execution chain.|
|parent_workflow_exec_id|string \| null|true|none|Execution ID of the parent workflow that initiated this execution. If this is a root workflow, this field is not set.|
|continued_run_id|string \| null|false|none|Run ID of the execution this run continued from. Non-null for continue-as-new runs.|
|first_execution_run_id|string \| null|false|none|Run ID of the first execution in this workflow chain. Equals workflow_run_id on a fresh start. Continue-as-new, retry and reset runs keep the original value.|
|chain_run_id|string \| null|false|none|Identifies one start of an execution. Shared by its continue-as-new, retry and reset runs, and by every sub-workflow below it. Starting the same execution ID again gives a new value.|
|schedule_id|string \| null|false|none|Temporal schedule ID that triggered this execution, if any.|
|workflow_exec_id|string|true|none|Execution ID of the workflow that emitted this event.|
|workflow_run_id|string|true|none|Run ID of the workflow execution. Changes on continue-as-new while workflow_exec_id stays the same.|
|workflow_name|string|true|none|The registered name of the workflow that emitted this event.|
|event_type|string|true|none|Event type discriminator.|
|attributes|[WorkflowExecutionCanceledAttributes](#schemaworkflowexecutioncanceledattributes)|true|none|Event-specific attributes.|

<h2 id="tocS_WorkflowExecutionStartedResponse">WorkflowExecutionStartedResponse</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaworkflowexecutionstartedresponse"></a>
<a id="schema_WorkflowExecutionStartedResponse"></a>
<a id="tocSworkflowexecutionstartedresponse"></a>
<a id="tocsworkflowexecutionstartedresponse"></a>

```json
{
  "event_id": "string",
  "event_timestamp": 0,
  "root_workflow_exec_id": "string",
  "parent_workflow_exec_id": "string",
  "continued_run_id": "string",
  "first_execution_run_id": "string",
  "chain_run_id": "string",
  "schedule_id": "string",
  "workflow_exec_id": "string",
  "workflow_run_id": "string",
  "workflow_name": "string",
  "event_type": "WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_STARTED",
  "attributes": {
    "task_id": "string",
    "workflow_name": "string",
    "display_name": "string",
    "input": {
      "type": "json",
      "value": null,
      "encoding_options": [
        "offloaded"
      ]
    },
    "attempt": 1
  }
}
```

Emitted when a workflow execution begins.

This is the first event in any workflow execution lifecycle.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|event_id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for this event instance.|
|event_timestamp|integer|true|none|Unix timestamp in nanoseconds when the event was created.|
|root_workflow_exec_id|string|true|none|Execution ID of the root workflow that initiated this execution chain.|
|parent_workflow_exec_id|string \| null|true|none|Execution ID of the parent workflow that initiated this execution. If this is a root workflow, this field is not set.|
|continued_run_id|string \| null|false|none|Run ID of the execution this run continued from. Non-null for continue-as-new runs.|
|first_execution_run_id|string \| null|false|none|Run ID of the first execution in this workflow chain. Equals workflow_run_id on a fresh start. Continue-as-new, retry and reset runs keep the original value.|
|chain_run_id|string \| null|false|none|Identifies one start of an execution. Shared by its continue-as-new, retry and reset runs, and by every sub-workflow below it. Starting the same execution ID again gives a new value.|
|schedule_id|string \| null|false|none|Temporal schedule ID that triggered this execution, if any.|
|workflow_exec_id|string|true|none|Execution ID of the workflow that emitted this event.|
|workflow_run_id|string|true|none|Run ID of the workflow execution. Changes on continue-as-new while workflow_exec_id stays the same.|
|workflow_name|string|true|none|The registered name of the workflow that emitted this event.|
|event_type|string|true|none|Event type discriminator.|
|attributes|[WorkflowExecutionStartedAttributesResponse](#schemaworkflowexecutionstartedattributesresponse)|true|none|Event-specific attributes.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|task_id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the task within the workflow execution.|

|input|[JSONPayloadResponse](#schemajsonpayloadresponse)|true|none|The input arguments passed to the workflow.|
|attempt|integer|false|none|Workflow retry attempt number. 1 on first run and CAN; >1 on workflow-level retries.|

<h2 id="tocS_WorkflowTaskFailedResponse">WorkflowTaskFailedResponse</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaworkflowtaskfailedresponse"></a>
<a id="schema_WorkflowTaskFailedResponse"></a>
<a id="tocSworkflowtaskfailedresponse"></a>
<a id="tocsworkflowtaskfailedresponse"></a>

```json
{
  "event_id": "string",
  "event_timestamp": 0,
  "root_workflow_exec_id": "string",
  "parent_workflow_exec_id": "string",
  "continued_run_id": "string",
  "first_execution_run_id": "string",
  "chain_run_id": "string",
  "schedule_id": "string",
  "workflow_exec_id": "string",
  "workflow_run_id": "string",
  "workflow_name": "string",
  "event_type": "WORKFLOW_TASK_FAILED",
  "attributes": {
    "task_id": "string",
    "failure": {
      "message": "string"
    }
  }
}
```

Emitted when a workflow task fails.

This indicates an error occurred during workflow task execution,
which may trigger a retry depending on configuration.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|event_id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for this event instance.|
|event_timestamp|integer|true|none|Unix timestamp in nanoseconds when the event was created.|
|root_workflow_exec_id|string|true|none|Execution ID of the root workflow that initiated this execution chain.|
|parent_workflow_exec_id|string \| null|true|none|Execution ID of the parent workflow that initiated this execution. If this is a root workflow, this field is not set.|
|continued_run_id|string \| null|false|none|Run ID of the execution this run continued from. Non-null for continue-as-new runs.|
|first_execution_run_id|string \| null|false|none|Run ID of the first execution in this workflow chain. Equals workflow_run_id on a fresh start. Continue-as-new, retry and reset runs keep the original value.|
|chain_run_id|string \| null|false|none|Identifies one start of an execution. Shared by its continue-as-new, retry and reset runs, and by every sub-workflow below it. Starting the same execution ID again gives a new value.|
|schedule_id|string \| null|false|none|Temporal schedule ID that triggered this execution, if any.|
|workflow_exec_id|string|true|none|Execution ID of the workflow that emitted this event.|
|workflow_run_id|string|true|none|Run ID of the workflow execution. Changes on continue-as-new while workflow_exec_id stays the same.|
|workflow_name|string|true|none|The registered name of the workflow that emitted this event.|
|event_type|string|true|none|Event type discriminator.|
|attributes|[WorkflowTaskFailedAttributes](#schemaworkflowtaskfailedattributes)|true|none|Event-specific attributes.|

<h2 id="tocS_WhoamiResponse">WhoamiResponse</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemawhoamiresponse"></a>
<a id="schema_WhoamiResponse"></a>
<a id="tocSwhoamiresponse"></a>
<a id="tocswhoamiresponse"></a>

```json
{
  "principal": {
    "principal_type": "user",
    "id": "8f14e45f-ceea-4e0a-9b0e-8f7d3c2a1b4e",
    "email": "ada@example.com",
    "first_name": "Ada",
    "last_name": "Lovelace"
  },
  "customer_id": "3b241101-e2bb-4255-8caf-4136c566a962",
  "organization": {
    "id": "1a2b3c4d-5e6f-4a8b-9c0d-1e2f3a4b5c6d",
    "name": "Acme Corp",
    "org_tier": "E",
    "internal": false,
    "kind": "S"
  },
  "workspace": {
    "id": "string",
    "name": "string"
  }
}
```

Principal-agnostic identity of the authenticated caller.

Supersedes the user-centric ``/v1/users/me`` and ``/api/users/v2/me`` by
resolving any principal (user or service account) through a single call. The
``principal`` field is a discriminated union; the remaining fields are the
shared session context and apply to either principal kind.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|principal|[WhoamiUserPrincipal](#schemawhoamiuserprincipal) \| [WhoamiServiceAccountPrincipal](#schemawhoamiserviceaccountprincipal)|true|none|The authenticated principal: either a user or a service account.|
|customer_id|string \| null|false|none|The billing customer identifier from the authenticated session. Identifies the billing account, not the organization (organization.id); the IDs are not interchangeable. Null when no customer is selected.|
|organization|[WhoamiOrganization](#schemawhoamiorganization) \| null|false|none|The organization the caller's session is scoped to, when set.|
|workspace|[UserIdentityWorkspace](#schemauseridentityworkspace) \| null|false|none|The workspace the caller's session is scoped to, when set.|

<h2 id="tocS_WhoamiServiceAccountPrincipal">WhoamiServiceAccountPrincipal</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemawhoamiserviceaccountprincipal"></a>
<a id="schema_WhoamiServiceAccountPrincipal"></a>
<a id="tocSwhoamiserviceaccountprincipal"></a>
<a id="tocswhoamiserviceaccountprincipal"></a>

```json
{
  "principal_type": "service_account",
  "service_account_id": "3b241101-e2bb-4255-8caf-4136c566a962",
  "name": "ci-deploy-bot"
}
```

Identity of a service-account principal.

Carries service-account-only fields. Service accounts have no user profile
(no email or name of a person); ``name`` is the service account's own display
name. Resolved independently of the authentication mechanism.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|principal_type|string|false|none|Discriminator identifying a service-account principal.|
|service_account_id|string|true|none|The service account's unique identifier.|
|name|string \| null|false|none|The service account's display name, when known.|

<h2 id="tocS_WhoamiUserPrincipal">WhoamiUserPrincipal</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemawhoamiuserprincipal"></a>
<a id="schema_WhoamiUserPrincipal"></a>
<a id="tocSwhoamiuserprincipal"></a>
<a id="tocswhoamiuserprincipal"></a>

```json
{
  "principal_type": "user",
  "id": "8f14e45f-ceea-4e0a-9b0e-8f7d3c2a1b4e",
  "email": "ada@example.com",
  "first_name": "Ada",
  "last_name": "Lovelace"
}
```

Identity of a human user principal.

Carries user-only fields. The ``principal_type`` discriminator makes this
variant mutually exclusive with the service-account variant, so a payload can
never carry both a user id and a service-account id.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|principal_type|string|false|none|Discriminator identifying a human user principal.|
|id|string|true|none|The user's unique identifier.|
|email|string \| null|false|none|The user's email address, when known.|
|first_name|string \| null|false|none|The user's first name, when known.|
|last_name|string \| null|false|none|The user's last name, when known.|

|call_type|string \| null|false|none|Type of call within its source.|

<h2 id="tocS_UsageType">UsageType</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemausagetype"></a>
<a id="schema_UsageType"></a>
<a id="tocSusagetype"></a>
<a id="tocsusagetype"></a>

```json
"usage"
```

The UsageType maps a recorded usage to a billable metric in Lago.

For example `UsageType.COMPLETION` maps to `api_tokens` in Lago. A new UsageType is billed only once it is added to
`USAGE_TYPE_TO_LAGO_EVENT_TYPE_MAP` in kazekit.usage, which the job reporting the usage relies on. Types left out of
it, such as `WORKFLOW_EXECUTIONS`, are recorded but not reported to Lago.

<h2 id="tocS_APIKeyActions">APIKeyActions</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaapikeyactions"></a>
<a id="schema_APIKeyActions"></a>
<a id="tocSapikeyactions"></a>
<a id="tocsapikeyactions"></a>

```json
{
  "rotate": {
    "status": "available"
  },
  "delete": {
    "status": "available"
  }
}
```

Per-action availability for an API key, keyed by action name.

This is the generic, reusable shape for surfacing what a viewer may do with a resource on
get/list endpoints: each action maps to a value that is either available or unavailable with an
optional reason code. Add fields here as more actions are exposed.

Every action is opt-in: fields default to ``None`` (the action is absent), and an absent action
means "unavailable, with no specified reason". An action is only available when a producer
explicitly sets it to ``ActionAvailable``. This keeps permissions opt-in rather than opt-out, so
forgetting to populate an action can never accidentally expose it.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|rotate|[ActionAvailable](#schemaactionavailable) \| [ActionUnavailable_RotateUnavailableReason_](#schemaactionunavailable_rotateunavailablereason_) \| null|false|none|none|
|delete|[ActionAvailable](#schemaactionavailable) \| [ActionUnavailable_DeleteUnavailableReason_](#schemaactionunavailable_deleteunavailablereason_) \| null|false|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_DeleteUnavailableReason">DeleteUnavailableReason</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadeleteunavailablereason"></a>
<a id="schema_DeleteUnavailableReason"></a>
<a id="tocSdeleteunavailablereason"></a>
<a id="tocsdeleteunavailablereason"></a>

```json
"not_allowed"
```

Machine-readable reason why an API key cannot be deleted.

Deletion eligibility currently turns on a single request-scoped permission: whether the acting
user may delete (archive) the key. The reason is therefore determined where the acting user is
known (e.g. the dashboard), not from the key's scope or state. Consumers should treat unknown
values as "delete unavailable".

<h2 id="tocS_RotateUnavailableReason">RotateUnavailableReason</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemarotateunavailablereason"></a>
<a id="schema_RotateUnavailableReason"></a>
<a id="tocSrotateunavailablereason"></a>
<a id="tocsrotateunavailablereason"></a>

```json
"unsupported_scope"
```

Machine-readable reason why an API key cannot be rotated.

This is the single field shared across services to describe rotation eligibility. An absent
reason (None) means the key can be rotated; any value means it cannot, and identifies why so
consumers (e.g. the dashboard rotate button) can show an appropriate message without hardcoding
the rules. Consumers should treat unknown values as "rotation unavailable".

Key-state reasons depend on the key's own state (e.g. expiry) and are determined where the key
lives, e.g. Albe. Permission-based reasons are request-scoped (they depend on who is asking) and can
only be determined where the acting user is known, e.g. the dashboard. When both apply, the
key-state reason wins.

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|search_expression|string \| null|false|none|Filter expression. Trace fields (e.g. `service_name`, `error_count`, `models_used`) are evaluated on the aggregated trace. Span attribute fields (e.g. `temporalWorkflowID`, `wf.type`, `gen_ai.provider.name`) are evaluated on the spans of the trace: a trace matches when one of its spans matches. Span attribute conditions combined with AND must hold on the same span, e.g. `temporalWorkflowID = 'wf-1' AND wf.type = 'activity'` only matches traces with a span carrying both attributes. Results are always one row per trace.|

<a id="tocsconnectortoolcallresponse"></a>

```json
{
  "content": [
    {
      "type": "text",
      "text": "string",
      "annotations": {
        "audience": [
          "user"
        ],
        "priority": 0,
        "lastModified": "string"
      },
      "_meta": {}
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "mcp_meta": {
      "isError": false,
      "structuredContent": null,
      "_meta": {}
    }
  }
}
```

Response from calling an MCP tool.

We override mcp_types.CallToolResult because:
- Models only support `content`, not `structuredContent` at top level
- Downstream consumers (le-chat, etc.) need structuredContent/isError/_meta via metadata

SYNC: Keep in sync with Harmattan (orchestrator) for harmonized tool result processing.

|content|[[TextContent](#schematextcontent) \| [ImageContent](#schemaimagecontent) \| [AudioContent](#schemaaudiocontent) \| [ResourceLink](#schemaresourcelink) \| [EmbeddedResource](#schemaembeddedresource)]|true|none|none|
|metadata|[ConnectorToolCallMetadata](#schemaconnectortoolcallmetadata) \| null|false|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_CreateWebhook">CreateWebhook</h2>

<a id="tocscreatewebhook"></a>

```json
{
  "provider": "slack",
  "owner_type": "workspace",
  "name": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "secret": "stringstringstr",
  "encryption_key": "stringstringstr",
  "url_verification_token": "string",
  "expires_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "signature_hash_algorithm": "sha256",
  "signature_header_name": "string",
  "validity_period_second": 1,
  "signature_extractor_regex": "string",
  "timestamp_extractor_regex": "string",
  "timestamp_pattern": "string",
  "signature_payload_pattern": "string",
  "signature_encoding": "hex",
  "success_status_code": 200,
  "event_type_pattern": "string",
  "event_id_pattern": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|provider|[WebhookProvider](#schemawebhookprovider)|true|none|none|
|owner_type|[TriggersOwnerType](#schematriggersownertype)|false|none|none|
|name|string|true|none|Human-readable name for this webhook|
|description|string \| null|false|none|What this webhook is used for|
|secret|string \| null|false|none|Signing secret provided by the third-party provider|
|encryption_key|string \| null|false|none|Encryption key used to decrypt webhook payloads|
|url_verification_token|string \| null|false|none|Token the provider echoes back when verifying the URL. Required for WhatsApp (paste the same value in the Verify token field of the Meta App Dashboard), forbidden for other providers|
|expires_at|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|none|
|signature_hash_algorithm|[WebhookSignatureHashAlgorithm](#schemawebhooksignaturehashalgorithm) \| null|false|none|none|
|signature_header_name|string \| null|false|none|none|
|validity_period_second|integer \| null|false|none|Maximum allowed drift in seconds between the signed timestamp and reception time, eg 300|
|signature_extractor_regex|string \| null|false|none|Regex to extract signature, eg sha256=(.*)|
|timestamp_extractor_regex|string \| null|false|none|Regex to extract the timestamp from the rendered timestamp_pattern (the signature header by default), used as {timestamp}, eg t=([^,]+). Defaults to the whole value when timestamp_pattern is set|
|timestamp_pattern|string \| null|false|none|Pattern for the timestamp used as {timestamp}, with {body.&lt;path&gt;} and {headers.&lt;Header-Name&gt;} placeholders, eg {headers.X-Slack-Request-Timestamp} or {body.webhookTimestamp}. Defaults to the signature header when timestamp_extractor_regex is set|
|signature_payload_pattern|string \| null|false|none|Pattern for signature payload, eg {body} or {timestamp}.{body}|
|signature_encoding|[WebhookSignatureEncoding](#schemawebhooksignatureencoding) \| null|false|none|none|
|success_status_code|integer \| null|false|none|HTTP status code returned for accepted deliveries, eg 200|
|event_type_pattern|string \| null|false|none|Pattern for the event type, with {body.&lt;path&gt;} and {headers.&lt;Header-Name&gt;} placeholders, eg {body.type} or {headers.X-GitHub-Event}|
|event_id_pattern|string \| null|false|none|Pattern for a unique event identifier used to deduplicate deliveries, with {body.&lt;path&gt;} and {headers.&lt;Header-Name&gt;} placeholders, eg {body.id} or {body.event_id}.{headers.X-Delivery-Id}. Defaults to a hash of the request body|

|provider|linear|
|provider|microsoft|
|provider|ashby|
|provider|whatsapp|
|provider|custom|
|owner_type|workspace|
|owner_type|user|

<h2 id="tocS_BudgetDetail">BudgetDetail</h2>

<a id="schemabudgetdetail"></a>

```json
{
  "usage_percentage": 42.5,
  "initial_budget": 300,
  "currency": "EUR",
  "reset_at": "2026-08-01T00:00:00Z",
  "payg_enabled": false
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|usage_percentage|number|true|none|Percentage of the budget consumed for the requested billing period (0-100).|
|initial_budget|number|true|none|Initial budget allocated for the billing period, expressed in the budget currency.|
|currency|string \| null|false|none|ISO 4217 currency code of the budget (e.g. EUR, USD). The applicable budget is lazily materialized for the requested period, so this is only null when no budget could be derived.|
|reset_at|string(date-time)|true|none|Timestamp at which the requested billing period resets (start of the next period).|
|payg_enabled|boolean|false|none|Whether pay-as-you-go overage is enabled for this budget type. Only meaningful for the Vibe budget.|

<h2 id="tocS_GetSubscriptionResponse">GetSubscriptionResponse</h2>

```json
  "payg_enabled": false,
  "vibe_payg_enabled": false,
  "enterprise": false
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|plan_name|string|true|none|Unified plan name. One of: FREE, INDIVIDUAL, EDU, TEAM. Reflects the active Mistral licence (chat subscription) or FREE when no subscription exists.|

|vibe_payg_enabled|boolean|true|none|Whether pay-as-you-go is enabled for Vibe Code specifically.|
|enterprise|boolean|true|none|Whether the organization is on the Enterprise tier (org_tier == ENTERPRISE).|
